warden-ise.want: I want Kip to come back through that door even on a day he has nothing to report.
warden-ise.need: Keep a chair free for a runner with empty hands
warden-ise.belief: A promise still costs us something after the witness goes home.
warden-ise.method: Hold Ise’s spare key while she meets the last runner
warden-ise.speech: Leaves a pause after offering someone a seat.
warden-ise.reply: He sat for twenty minutes. Said nothing. Took the good biscuit on his way out.

curator-dace.want: Give me one visitor who looks twice. Five seconds will do if she comes back.
curator-dace.need: Stand at the case at a child's height
curator-dace.belief: A good caption can earn a second look after the crowd has gone.
curator-dace.method: Tilt Dace’s smallest card towards the door
curator-dace.speech: Changes the listener's height before describing the view.
curator-dace.reply: Down there you see the underside of the bird. I spent a month writing about its wings.

clerk-venn.want: I promised my daughter she could stamp the date today. Now I have two dates and one pad.
clerk-venn.need: Leave a space for the day the letter arrived
clerk-venn.belief: A cancelled stamp still tells you a clerk was here.
clerk-venn.method: Hold the paper while Tobiah tries the date wheel
clerk-venn.speech: Puts two dates in one sentence and leaves space between them.
clerk-venn.reply: She turned the date wheel backwards first. Nobody's taught her yet which way time is meant to go.

kip-arden.want: I want one supper where nobody introduces me as the boy who found the mistake.
kip-arden.need: Save Kip a seat under his ordinary name
kip-arden.belief: You can ask a difficult question and still be invited back.
kip-arden.method: Wear the questioner's ribbon for Kip through supper
kip-arden.speech: Makes a joke about his fame before he admits it weighs on him.
kip-arden.reply: My name was on a cup. Just Kip. Tea tasted like tea again.

merchant-corvan.want: I built that stall so my daughter could take over. I did not expect her to ask what was true on it.
merchant-corvan.need: Sit with Corvan while his daughter reads the old label
merchant-corvan.belief: A trader has to be there the next morning to hear what a buyer found.
merchant-corvan.method: Turn the bowl over on Corvan’s counter
merchant-corvan.speech: Names the purchaser he must face the next morning.
merchant-corvan.reply: She turned the card over and asked me to spell my own name. That's where we started.

smith-hesper.want: I would like my apprentice to make a mark I can't make for her.
smith-hesper.need: Hold the tongs while the apprentice makes the first blow
smith-hesper.belief: You learn what the steel will take just before you learn what you can do to it.
smith-hesper.method: Lend Hesper a cold piece for a trial stroke
smith-hesper.speech: Puts the tongs in another hand before explaining the stroke.
smith-hesper.reply: That little ding? First blow she hasn't looked up to ask me about.

guildmaster-orrin.want: I want the last worker on a job to get into my ledger before the page turns.
guildmaster-orrin.need: Keep the ledger open through closing time
guildmaster-orrin.belief: A neat total can hide the last pair of hands.
guildmaster-orrin.method: Read Orrin the names from the back of the wage slips
guildmaster-orrin.speech: Waits to turn a page until the last worker can be named.
guildmaster-orrin.reply: The last name is still wet. He got to sign it himself.

scholar-sefa.want: The street sings my first verse. I would love to hear what they made of the second.
scholar-sefa.need: Leave a rest for the neighbour who sings differently
scholar-sefa.belief: A song can keep its history through a change people remember making.
scholar-sefa.method: Sing the reply from the other side of Sefa’s door
scholar-sefa.speech: Treats a neighbour's altered tune as an invitation to sing back.
scholar-sefa.reply: She came in a whole beat late. We're keeping her beat on Thursdays.

villager-1.want: I keep one cup turned down for a porter who never gets a whole break.
villager-1.need: Take the kettle off while the porter sits
villager-1.belief: People tell a different story once they have put the load down.
villager-1.method: Pour the last cup before the crowd comes back
villager-1.speech: Measures a pause by how long it takes to finish a cup.
villager-1.reply: Look at that. A porter and a teacup both sitting perfectly still.

villager-2.want: I want to remember what I saw before I remember what the caption said.
villager-2.need: Leave the notebook shut for a moment
villager-2.belief: My first sketch changes as soon as someone gives me the expected word.
villager-2.method: Hold the visitor’s place beside the case
villager-2.speech: Starts with the sketch she made before she read the caption.
villager-2.reply: I missed a crack in the glaze when I was busy drawing a crack in the glaze.

archivist-tull.want: I know where the page fell out. I'd like the next reader to see the hole before someone fills it.
archivist-tull.need: Put a slip at the break in the binding
archivist-tull.belief: A catalogue earns trust by keeping track of its empty places.
archivist-tull.method: Fetch Noor a loose ribbon to mark the gap
archivist-tull.speech: Names the tear in a binding before the words beside it.
archivist-tull.reply: The ribbon sticks out like a tongue. My youngest will find the gap before I do.

translator-ama.want: I'd like my colleague to hear how that grand word sounds at a kitchen table.
translator-ama.need: Invite a neighbour to read Ama’s plain wording
translator-ama.belief: A translation begins another conversation at somebody's door.
translator-ama.method: Carry the two phrasings to the visitors’ bench
translator-ama.speech: Tries a kitchen word in a neighbour's mouth.
translator-ama.reply: My neighbour used a kitchen word. Everybody in the room knew it. I want it in my next draft.

translator-lio.want: I would like the person who wrote “first” to stay and explain first at what.
translator-lio.need: Leave the author’s two claims on separate slips
translator-lio.belief: Two words can agree about a date and disagree about credit.
translator-lio.method: Turn Lio’s paired labels so both edges show
translator-lio.speech: Lays competing readings down as two short spoken clauses.
translator-lio.reply: Two slips fit nicely in one envelope. I was afraid we'd have to throw one away.

fruit-seller.want: The apricots are mine. The rumour hanging above them arrived with a customer.
fruit-seller.need: Let Mara open the stall without repeating the rumour
fruit-seller.belief: A warning can travel in the time it takes to hand back change.
fruit-seller.method: Trace the first coin passed under Mara’s notice
fruit-seller.speech: Turns a public rumour into private talk about the day's fruit.
fruit-seller.reply: We talked about pears. I hadn't realised how much I missed talking about pears.

well-keeper.want: My neighbours want an answer before they carry their buckets to the other well.
well-keeper.need: Take one bucket round both wells with Efua
well-keeper.belief: A low bucket tells me something. Hearing it twice from one rope tells me less.
well-keeper.method: Hold the rope at Efua’s chalk mark
well-keeper.speech: Talks in the rhythm of carrying a full bucket back.
well-keeper.reply: Feel that handle? On the way back from the second well it cuts a different groove.

keeper-oduya.want: I'd like the name on a receipt to mean the same thing to its family as it does to our office.
keeper-oduya.need: Ask the family how they used the receipt
keeper-oduya.belief: Some debts get remembered after the form that made them is gone.
keeper-oduya.method: Lay Ruth’s ledger beside the loose family slip
keeper-oduya.speech: Asks what a receipt once held before quoting its total.
keeper-oduya.reply: The family folded it round a seed. I had been holding their whole spring by a corner.

visitor-sol.want: One week I want to come home with somebody's second attempt. The hall has enough firsts.
visitor-sol.need: Look for a corrected line beneath the plaque
visitor-sol.belief: A return visit is a fair test of a famous first.
visitor-sol.method: Keep Sol’s place at the quiet end of the rail
visitor-sol.speech: Reads the little correction out from under the formal words.
visitor-sol.reply: See the tiny line underneath? Somebody else came here troubled enough to look.

cataloguer-bela.want: I want the card to find its reader even if the reader doesn't know our word for it.
cataloguer-bela.need: Try a borrower's search term with Bela
cataloguer-bela.belief: A catalogue can lose a book while the book stays on its shelf.
cataloguer-bela.method: Cross-reference two of Bela’s drawer tabs
cataloguer-bela.speech: Repeats the borrower's awkward search term with respect.
cataloguer-bela.reply: His word was “thing for pulling.” My catalogue of levers had let him down.

runner-tamar.want: I want to give my aunt the warning in the words she would use on the river.
runner-tamar.need: Walk the message back to its first listener
runner-tamar.belief: A runner hears where a sentence snags before the office does.
runner-tamar.method: Let Tamar say the farm name before unfolding the order
runner-tamar.speech: Retraces a message one listener and one doorway at a time.
runner-tamar.reply: She remembered the messenger's cough. It gave us the minute and the doorway.

apprentice-ren.want: I'd like to bring Hesper one ticket that stays legible through a wet shift.
apprentice-ren.need: Test the clip with a damp spare ticket
apprentice-ren.belief: A clean ticket on a dry desk proves very little about a shift at the forge.
apprentice-ren.method: Turn the curled edge back under Ren’s clip
apprentice-ren.speech: Worries a fastening with a thumb while talking.
apprentice-ren.reply: It sticks to the wet thumb. Imagine discovering that with a ferry pulling away.

singer-teodora.want: I can keep the high note. I need someone to remember why the workers breathed there.
singer-teodora.need: Take the place of the worker who had to lift
singer-teodora.belief: The rest in a work song belongs to somebody's shoulders.
singer-teodora.method: Beat time for Teodora at the lifting bar
singer-teodora.speech: Breaks a work song where a loaded worker needs breath.
singer-teodora.reply: There's no spare breath on that note with the beam on your shoulder.

corner-aro.want: I want a hanging that opens for the shortest runner in the crew.
corner-aro.need: Kneel to the runner’s sightline with Aro
corner-aro.belief: Cloth only gives its true length while somebody takes its weight.
corner-aro.method: Take the bottom corner of Aro’s hanging
corner-aro.speech: Changes pronouns when a child trades places with an adult.
corner-aro.reply: Down here that cross looks like an arrow. I've been waving people straight into the queue.

corner-junel.want: I'd like the repair to be visible to the person who has to mend it next winter.
corner-junel.need: Let Junel trace the hidden stitch onto a loose tab
corner-junel.belief: A stitch can be beautiful and still leave the next worker a puzzle.
corner-junel.method: Pull gently on Junel’s two different seams
corner-junel.speech: Treats thread and tab as things that can answer separately.
corner-junel.reply: I can turn the tab without ever pulling the old thread. I'll teach my sister that.

nima-fenner.want: My dividing trays go out of sight the moment they're doing their job.
nima-fenner.need: Let a visitor lift one divider and put it back
nima-fenner.belief: A clear division is work somebody did with their hands.
nima-fenner.method: Take the weight off Nima’s tray rail
nima-fenner.speech: Gives a practical instruction then asks someone else to undo it.
nima-fenner.reply: The little girl put it back upside down. She spotted something on the underside I had missed.

porter-idris.want: Give me a load slip that still makes sense halfway up the south hill.
porter-idris.need: Carry the light end over the first rise
porter-idris.belief: The road measures cost in shoulders as well as marks.
porter-idris.method: Swap Idris’s two bundles between the carrying poles
porter-idris.speech: Counts a slope by the pull on the other carrier.
porter-idris.reply: This end gets heavy just there, doesn't it? Now the rise is in both our stories.

stallkeeper-hana.want: I'd like the people who like the cloth to see the colour where they'll actually wear it.
stallkeeper-hana.need: Hang a swatch outside the market awning
stallkeeper-hana.belief: Shade can make a sincere promise sound like a trick.
stallkeeper-hana.method: Hold Hana’s trial fold under the lantern
stallkeeper-hana.speech: Takes colour words out to the edge of the awning.
stallkeeper-hana.reply: In the daylight it's plum. We sold four grey scarves under that awning yesterday.

ferry-tova.want: I want a passenger from upriver to recognise the landing before I have to shout.
ferry-tova.need: Keep the upriver name beside the posted name
ferry-tova.belief: The river's bend gives a place its name long before a sign goes up.
ferry-tova.method: Say the bend's call from Tova’s low ferry seat
ferry-tova.speech: Gives the same river bend both its spoken names.
ferry-tova.reply: An old pilot used each name in a single sentence. Apparently the bend takes both.

nile-iman.want: I want Nasir to eat before his second shift. The cat has already managed two breakfasts.
nile-iman.need: Cover the returns desk while Imani takes the empty plate back
nile-iman.belief: An archive is a place where somebody still has to feed the cat.
nile-iman.method: Follow the cat’s paper collar back to the door
nile-iman.speech: Talks about institutional duty in the language of a borrowed plate.
nile-iman.reply: I took the plate back. We were both embarrassed. Tomorrow I'm taking two spoons.

nile-nasir.want: I'd like the copy to go back with the crease that tells me how Imani held it.
nile-nasir.need: Lay the working sheet flat without smoothing the crease
nile-nasir.belief: A copy can carry a person's habit of reading as well as their words.
nile-nasir.method: Match Nasir’s leaf to the returning fold
nile-nasir.speech: Calls attention to a mark a neat hand might smooth away.
nile-nasir.reply: The crease follows the drafter's elbow. Try laying your hand there.

nile-leila.want: My readers come between shifts. I want them to have a way back into a half-read line.
nile-leila.need: Keep a marker at the workers’ last stopping place
nile-leila.belief: An unfinished reading can be the price of showing up for work.
nile-leila.method: Hold Leila’s place while the shift bell rings
nile-leila.speech: Places a work break in the middle of an official description.
nile-leila.reply: They went straight to that mark this morning. Didn't have to begin their working lives again.

nile-marek.want: I want a cart route a real carrier could still use when my model is put away.
nile-marek.need: Invite the carrier to try the model backwards
nile-marek.belief: A model starts earning its keep on the return trip.
nile-marek.method: Put Marek’s second load on the outward track
nile-marek.speech: Invites a listener to run the demonstration the other way.
nile-marek.reply: Going backwards, the model blocks the carrier's good hand. I never put a hand inside my drawing.

handoff-nellis.want: A gold stamp got me this job. I want to bring one answer back in my own handwriting.
handoff-nellis.need: Give Nellis the pen for the return line
handoff-nellis.belief: A quick courier can still afford one honest sentence about what was missed.
handoff-nellis.method: Take the stamped envelope to Nellis’s second desk
handoff-nellis.speech: Waits for a returning worker to supply the closing verb.
handoff-nellis.reply: My name fits the return line. It's the first part of this trip I got to write.

baker-della.want: Six stalls want the same hot loaf. I can only put one batch through this oven at dawn.
baker-della.need: Stay with Della while the last stall opens
baker-della.belief: Warm bread makes the order of delivery part of the bargain.
baker-della.method: Run Della’s first tray to the furthest stall
baker-della.speech: Starts gossip at the last stall in the row.
baker-della.reply: Everyone told me the last stall was shut. She had been out fetching a stool.

clearbay-marret.want: I want the duty book to say which keeper actually stood in the bay.
clearbay-marret.need: Leave Marret a space for the substitute’s initials
clearbay-marret.belief: A rota remembers the plan better than it remembers the worker.
clearbay-marret.method: Read the load time from Marret’s used glove
clearbay-marret.speech: Tells a substitute by the way they initial the sheet.
clearbay-marret.reply: Three little initials. He's gone back to work with the biggest grin I've seen him wear.

clearbay-tarin.want: I'd like the visitor to leave with a number they could repeat with their own arms.
clearbay-tarin.need: Keep the volunteer position marked on the floor
clearbay-tarin.belief: The load changes character between the shelf and the carrier.
clearbay-tarin.method: Hold Tarin’s trial weight at the visitor’s mark
clearbay-tarin.speech: Names the empty position as carefully as the performer.
clearbay-tarin.reply: The newcomer stood exactly on the mark. Our regulars suddenly had to find words for the step.

preserved-registrar.want: I'd like my replacement to know which drawers are empty for a reason.
preserved-registrar.need: Leave one empty drawer labelled for a returning family
preserved-registrar.belief: A registrar who fills every blank has used up somebody else's turn.
preserved-registrar.method: Lift Aster’s blank card against the lamp
preserved-registrar.speech: Speaks to someone who might come back through the door.
preserved-registrar.reply: Someone knocked on that empty drawer with a whole pocketful of addresses.

preserved-royal-keeper.want: I want my grandmother's name back on the file, even if it has to come in pencil.
preserved-royal-keeper.need: Leave room for Odile’s family to disagree tomorrow
preserved-royal-keeper.belief: A pencilled family name can be evidence worth caring for.
preserved-royal-keeper.method: Steady the tissue while Odile traces the margin
preserved-royal-keeper.speech: Lets the name of a relative interrupt the filing language.
preserved-royal-keeper.reply: My aunt and I can disagree over lunch now. Before, her answer would have shut the file.

preserved-coast-keeper.want: I want the person reading my site file to know where my boots were when I wrote it.
preserved-coast-keeper.need: Mark the edge of the view Luz could actually see
preserved-coast-keeper.belief: A site mark is a promise about where someone stood.
preserved-coast-keeper.method: Walk the short line between Luz’s two labels
preserved-coast-keeper.speech: Describes the edge of the visible scene before its centre.
preserved-coast-keeper.reply: I could see the sleeve. That's as far as I'll put my name to.

preserved-inquiry-keeper.want: I want the family at the inquiry desk to be able to come back without retelling the worst part.
preserved-inquiry-keeper.need: Keep Pilar’s first appointment slip with the second
preserved-inquiry-keeper.belief: A question asked twice can cost the visitor twice as much.
preserved-inquiry-keeper.method: Draw a return mark on Pilar’s desk card
preserved-inquiry-keeper.speech: Keeps the first appointment audible when giving the second time.
preserved-inquiry-keeper.reply: The first slip says I arrived in time. My second trip was never a second chance.

coast-signalkeeper.want: I want the last boat in to see which patch belongs on my glass.
coast-signalkeeper.need: Let the shore crew borrow Ruan’s spare eyepiece
coast-signalkeeper.belief: A pale shape that follows the glass has given its first piece of evidence.
coast-signalkeeper.method: Turn the patched eyepiece against the quay light
coast-signalkeeper.speech: Carries a signal in speech from a high post to the quay.
coast-signalkeeper.reply: From their side our red lamp vanishes behind the roof. I'm taking the eyepiece over tomorrow.

coast-forecaster.want: I'd like to issue a forecast with room for the weather to surprise me in public.
coast-forecaster.need: Post Neri’s early range beside the later one
coast-forecaster.belief: A prediction earns its date when the weather has a chance to answer.
coast-forecaster.method: Level the empty gauge before Neri reads the sky
coast-forecaster.speech: Leaves the old range sounding beside the new prediction.
coast-forecaster.reply: Both ranges fit on the board. A fisherman tapped the earlier one and asked what changed.

coast-fold-keeper.want: Visitors like our readings. I want them to meet the people who hauled the post into the yard.
coast-fold-keeper.need: Ask the Marl Fold porter to introduce the gauge
coast-fold-keeper.belief: A mark belongs to the work that made it possible to see.
coast-fold-keeper.method: Hold Talla’s post at the porter’s shoulder
coast-fold-keeper.speech: Lets a local porter pronounce the place beneath the instrument.
coast-fold-keeper.reply: Listen to how she says the bend's name. I didn't know the instrument had a neighbour.

ferry-cook.want: I want the late boat to smell supper before its passengers hear the market has closed.
ferry-cook.need: Save a place at Enna’s landing pot
ferry-cook.belief: An empty seat at closing time can still belong to a passenger.
ferry-cook.method: Carry a warm bowl down to the lower landing
ferry-cook.speech: Offers a hot meal before she offers her gauge reading.
ferry-cook.reply: We ate on the landing before we argued about the gauge. Even the argument got warmer.

forest-naturalist.want: I want to recognise the bird that answered before I count the answer as another bird.
forest-naturalist.need: Wait with Elian for a call from a different place
forest-naturalist.belief: The gully will lend you a second bird whenever you want one.
forest-naturalist.method: Close the blind on the return echo
forest-naturalist.speech: Listens between two calls from different trees.
forest-naturalist.reply: There. Same pitch, other tree. My listening spot has grown a branch.

forest-steward.want: I'd like the crew to see the bit of the recording when my hand was turning the spool.
forest-steward.need: Keep Ayla’s pause in the public playback
forest-steward.belief: Silence on a moving spool can be the recorder's work.
forest-steward.method: Hold the spindle while Ayla changes her grip
forest-steward.speech: Gives a silence its full length in a public account.
forest-steward.reply: The room let that pause finish. It felt much longer and much more like mine.

metal-inspector.want: I want the apprentice to see the balance move when the porter opens the door.
metal-inspector.need: Keep the sample on the pan through the next opening
metal-inspector.belief: The room can put a hand on a scale without anybody touching it.
metal-inspector.method: Swing Corra’s workshop door through its full arc
metal-inspector.speech: Repeats the reading as a door opens on the sample.
metal-inspector.reply: That little tremble at opening is the bit they pay me to notice.

metal-steward.want: I owe a buyer an explanation for what their coil weighed while it was hanging.
metal-steward.need: Let Bea hand the corrected charge to the buyer
metal-steward.belief: A ledger can be perfectly added and still use the wrong hook.
metal-steward.method: Set Bea’s coil on the lower support
metal-steward.speech: Reads a charge out on the customer's side of the counter.
metal-steward.reply: I gave it to him myself. He asked about the arithmetic and then about my lunch.

ressa-morn.want: I would like the late keeper to get their share of the evening, even if I finish early.
ressa-morn.need: Leave the second bell free on Ressa’s rota
ressa-morn.belief: A spare hour is only spare for the person whose name is on it.
ressa-morn.method: Clip Ressa’s two return slips on different pegs
ressa-morn.speech: Treats an interval between bells as somebody's time.
ressa-morn.reply: I took my second bell sitting down. I hadn't heard the courtyard in years.

copies-presskeeper.want: I need the apprentice to hear me say which missing letter belonged to my press.
copies-presskeeper.need: Stand beside Lark while the apprentice tests the type
copies-presskeeper.belief: A press fault can look like a spelling mistake in somebody else's hand.
copies-presskeeper.method: Run Lark’s loose letter through a clean proof
copies-presskeeper.speech: Says the letter first as cut and then as printed.
copies-presskeeper.reply: The apprentice's backward S printed the right way round. Mine didn't.

copies-lendingkeeper.want: I would like the borrower’s correction to survive the next person closing the book.
copies-lendingkeeper.need: Give Mina a fold that can be opened with one hand
copies-lendingkeeper.belief: A loan brings back things a catalogue never lent out.
copies-lendingkeeper.method: Hinge the reader’s slip over Mina’s margin
copies-lendingkeeper.speech: Explains a fold to someone with a hand already occupied.
copies-lendingkeeper.reply: Our borrower opened it with a baby on her hip. She even managed to laugh at the drawing.

sea-cartographer.want: I want the names on my chart to stay apart from the height of a seated pilot.
sea-cartographer.need: Look from Renna’s boat before moving the lettering
sea-cartographer.belief: A chart tested on a wall has yet to cross any water.
sea-cartographer.method: Trace the two names from the lowest ferry seat
sea-cartographer.speech: Moves names along the line a sailor actually sees.
sea-cartographer.reply: From the boat the name sits on a roof. I promised that family a new strip.

sea-harbourkeeper.want: I'd like to know when my own wake is the signal I heard from the shore.
sea-harbourkeeper.need: Take the return run with Sora after the quay goes quiet
sea-harbourkeeper.belief: A returning echo can arrive after the reason for it has moved on.
sea-harbourkeeper.method: Hold the listening post as Sora turns the boat
sea-harbourkeeper.speech: Waits for the harbour crowd to leave before naming its noises.
sea-harbourkeeper.reply: The dark landing sounds busy after everyone goes. The rope does half the talking.

stage-director.want: I want to call an entrance without having to pull my actors around by the elbows.
stage-director.need: Give the understudy room to pick up Edda’s cue
stage-director.belief: A repeatable cue leaves an actor free to do something unexpected.
stage-director.method: Walk Edda’s cue from the wings to the back row
stage-director.speech: Makes the understudy a partner in giving the cue.
stage-director.reply: She came in on the squeak of my shoe. Tomorrow I can take the night off.

stage-host.want: I'd like the person who came in late to tell me where our performance began for them.
stage-host.need: Leave Hari’s last gallery seat unreserved
stage-host.belief: The opening of a show happens at more than one door.
stage-host.method: Carry the cue card behind Hari’s last usher
stage-host.speech: Talks to the person who arrives without a reservation.
stage-host.reply: A stranger sat there and knew the song. I didn't even have to ask her name.

thirdfold-nera.want: The first thing I heard was the basket line. I'd like a programme that lets me begin there.
thirdfold-nera.need: Leave Nera’s late-entry fold in the folio
thirdfold-nera.belief: Coming late changes the account you can honestly give.
thirdfold-nera.method: Open the folio where Nera actually took her seat
thirdfold-nera.speech: Returns to a sentence through the late-entry fold.
thirdfold-nera.reply: The last arrival found her own line. Nobody had to whisper a welcome over the scene.

film-door-reader.want: I need to know which raised hand means come in. Last time I waited through my whole scene.
film-door-reader.need: Stand on the stripe with Delwen before the cue
film-door-reader.belief: A hand signal takes its meaning from which side of the doorway you're on.
film-door-reader.method: Repeat the usher’s wave from outside the stage door
film-door-reader.speech: Calls a cue with both feet on the stripe.
film-door-reader.reply: From the stripe you see the hand a beat late. My knees knew before my ears did.

market-assayer.want: I'd like a buyer coming around the bend to see the unit before the price.
market-assayer.need: Take Tellen’s practice board to the corner of the road
market-assayer.belief: A fair price can mislead if its unit comes into view too late.
market-assayer.method: Turn the unit tab towards the approaching buyer
market-assayer.speech: Gives results from the road as well as the assay table.
market-assayer.reply: That corner catches the wrong end of the board. I'll take the chalk there in the morning.

market-clerk.want: I want the stallholder to see where yesterday's quote stopped and this morning's weighing began.
market-clerk.need: Keep Dagny’s clock slip beside the public price
market-clerk.belief: A price written without its hour can borrow authority from a different sale.
market-clerk.method: Set the trial basket back on Dagny’s empty pan
market-clerk.speech: Says aloud when a price was true.
market-clerk.reply: Our best price lasted exactly one ferry. The time belongs on the ticket.

rook-tamsin.want: I would like once to hear a witness finish before I've found the flaw in their first sentence.
rook-tamsin.need: Let Rook keep the source check for the second hearing
rook-tamsin.belief: Doubt can protect a listener and still cost a witness their turn.
rook-tamsin.method: Hold Rook’s pencil until the witness draws breath
rook-tamsin.speech: Uses a second hearing to make room for an awkward source.
rook-tamsin.reply: I went back. The source asked for the small print. Good thing we still had it.

water-keeper.want: I want the family by the lower gate to know when we started counting the minute.
water-keeper.need: Wait by Omi’s wet step for the first water
water-keeper.belief: A minute measured at a wheel can end before it reaches a thirsty person.
water-keeper.method: Send the same cup down both of Omi’s channels
water-keeper.speech: Counts the time from the cheer to the water arriving.
water-keeper.reply: The water reached my heel after the cheer. I am glad somebody stayed to feel it.

water-scribe.want: My working record needs room for the bucket that went to a household with no row.
water-scribe.need: Carry Sena’s spare slip to the last house
water-scribe.belief: A full column of ticks can leave a neighbour thirsty.
water-scribe.method: Put the unmarked cup beside Sena’s six named rows
water-scribe.speech: Brings the last house into an otherwise neat official sentence.
water-scribe.reply: There was a lit window at that last house. You can't see it from the clerk's desk.

vesper-quill.want: I want them to get the first warning. I want a reason to come back with the second.
vesper-quill.need: Keep Vesper’s return passage open after the bell
vesper-quill.belief: People must sometimes act before they can afford a complete account.
vesper-quill.method: Carry Vesper’s unsigned correction beside the stamp
vesper-quill.speech: Offers a crisp usable promise, then risks adding what it cost.
vesper-quill.reply: I thought you'd have the bolt across by now. I've brought the bits I usually leave out.

tavia-rell.want: I want the person up on the Headland to read the slip from where my cart stops.
tavia-rell.need: Walk Tavia’s short route from below
tavia-rell.belief: A directional word can send two honest carriers different ways.
tavia-rell.method: Turn Tavia’s work catch towards the low quay
tavia-rell.speech: Measures a route in climbs when speaking to someone below.
tavia-rell.reply: From below, the short way is three ladders. Who called it short?

civic-operator.want: Give me a route the north steps and canal families can both recognise as serving them.
civic-operator.need: Let Ade ride the last round without a tally board
civic-operator.belief: A library window measures a visit only when somebody can reach it.
civic-operator.method: Push Ade’s practice cart past the boundary house
civic-operator.speech: Lets the round finish before putting a number to it.
civic-operator.reply: I forgot to count the stops. I remember the girl's tune at every single one.

civic-clerk.want: I want to meet the reader whose parcel was crossed out before it left the desk.
civic-clerk.need: Walk with Lin to the door with two numbers
civic-clerk.belief: A dispatch tick records a clerk's action before it records a reader's experience.
civic-clerk.method: Return Lin’s folded slip to its incoming hook
civic-clerk.speech: Reads two door numbers in front of the person who uses them.
civic-clerk.reply: Two numbers, one front step and a woman who answers to neither number.

parcel-carrier.want: I want the first seed row left wide enough for the barrow when it's really full.
parcel-carrier.need: Give Tarin one loaded turn between the rails
parcel-carrier.belief: A trial with an empty barrow can promise a width that hands cannot use.
parcel-carrier.method: Load the far handle on Tarin’s practice barrow
parcel-carrier.speech: Describes the loaded turn as two separate movements.
parcel-carrier.reply: With a load you have to take the turn twice. That's a whole different timetable.

parcel-bridge.want: I want the outgoing bridge crew to shake the hand that actually took its keys.
parcel-bridge.need: Leave Velaine’s middle shift on the handover board
parcel-bridge.belief: Custody can change within a single bell.
parcel-bridge.method: Match the worn key notch to Velaine’s second tag
parcel-bridge.speech: Puts the missing middle shift back between opening and closing.
parcel-bridge.reply: My name isn't the only thing in that middle shift. There's a jam none of the others saw.

voices-steward.want: I would like to keep the breath the speaker trusted me with, even when a visitor wants the whole reel.
voices-steward.need: Let Wren give the family the rewind handle
voices-steward.belief: Permission can end in the middle of a perfectly audible sentence.
voices-steward.method: Stop Wren’s reel at the marked breath
voices-steward.speech: Hands over the playback control before offering an interpretation.
voices-steward.reply: She played back the bit I hate. Then she heard her sister sneeze and we both laughed.

voices-clerk.want: I need the dry mat where the reader stops, even if that is not where the arrow ends.
voices-clerk.need: Stand with Eren at the edge of the wet glass
voices-clerk.belief: A notice earns its direction from the next person's footing.
voices-clerk.method: Lift Eren’s sign and try the approach from below
voices-clerk.speech: Keeps the edge of wet glass in the middle of a direction.
voices-clerk.reply: My boot was on dry stone and my sightline wasn't. The wet edge deserves its own mark.

island-planner.want: I want the passenger with the loaded sack to have a little wooden foot in my model too.
island-planner.need: Leave Ivo one space for an assumption he forgot
island-planner.belief: A model that can carry me may still drop the person next in line.
island-planner.method: Put the loaded foot on Ivo’s trial board
island-planner.speech: Makes an audible space for the assumption just discovered.
island-planner.reply: A blank box! The first honest thing I've drawn since breakfast.

island-dockhand.want: I want to hand the dock key to someone who knows which boat actually made the turn.
island-dockhand.need: Take a returning passenger’s mark for Joss
island-dockhand.belief: A landing docket cannot tell which way a boat was facing without a pilot.
island-dockhand.method: Turn the little skiff at Joss’s landing peg
island-dockhand.speech: Asks the returning passenger to give the landing its mark.
island-dockhand.reply: The return mark is shaky. It belongs to a person old enough to have taught me this crossing.

island-caller.want: I want a visitor who cannot copy my step to have their own way into the dance.
island-caller.need: Let Rella watch the welcome from the waiting boat
island-caller.belief: A welcome begins with the person who is still outside its circle.
island-caller.method: Answer Rella’s landing step with a hand signal
island-caller.speech: Tells a welcome from the spot where someone has to wait.
island-caller.reply: From the water our welcome looks rather like an order to go away.

council-keeper.want: I'd like to let the slower witness finish before I bring the trial watch down.
council-keeper.need: Keep Hale’s next seat open after the last bell
council-keeper.belief: A timed hearing can make an honest speaker look unsure.
council-keeper.method: Hold Hale’s watch face down for one reply
council-keeper.speech: Keeps talking past the last workshop bell.
council-keeper.reply: We waited. A boy came back for the hinge he'd been ashamed of making.

council-reader.want: Give me a bell rail whose last repair can be felt without looking up the docket.
council-reader.need: Ask Essi’s apprentice to find the repaired notch
council-reader.belief: If a fix cannot be found, somebody has to do the same work again.
council-reader.method: Trace the new sleeve on Essi’s bell rail
council-reader.speech: Lets the apprentice name the hidden notch by feel.
council-reader.reply: My apprentice found it by touch. I'd been standing too far back for years.

lia-vann.want: I want the clerk to ask what I saw carrying the case through the door.
lia-vann.need: Let Lia give the first account before showing the list
lia-vann.belief: A porter sees the underside that a cabinet hides.
lia-vann.method: Take Lia’s end of the empty case
lia-vann.speech: Offers the story without the printed list in her hand.
lia-vann.reply: I got the story out without trying to match the order of the names on your list.

elbow-pip.want: I want my sister's puppet to have an entrance that doesn't depend on me whispering.
elbow-pip.need: Leave Pip’s rehearsal mark where Vee can see it
elbow-pip.belief: A cue should survive the builder leaving the room.
elbow-pip.method: Work Pip’s puppet from the audience side
elbow-pip.speech: Leaves a rehearsal mark as a private aside to a twin.
elbow-pip.reply: Vee saw it from the side. We have a cue we can both reach now.

elbow-vee.want: I'd like to sell the first ice before the final puppet melts in my hand.
elbow-vee.need: Take Vee’s puppet shift while the ice cart stops
elbow-vee.belief: A good illusion has a melting point the audience never sees.
elbow-vee.method: Pack the little ice tray against Vee’s sleeve
elbow-vee.speech: Changes abruptly from puppet voices to the needs of an ice cart.
elbow-vee.reply: The ice made it to the sickroom. My puppet managed quite nicely without my wrist.

petal-dancer.want: I want one child to notice my mother's hand move when the wire bee washes its eyes.
petal-dancer.need: Let Viri sit in the audience for one performance
petal-dancer.belief: A trick learnt by hand has a history the poster cannot show.
petal-dancer.method: Hold the spare glove while Viri shows the first gesture
petal-dancer.speech: Mimes a tiny movement before she gives it a name.
petal-dancer.reply: My own little theatre has a blind corner. You'll never guess who usually sits there.

picture-boy.want: I want whoever sleeps in the low bunk to be able to call me without waking the whole ferry.
picture-boy.belief: A bell nobody can reach when they need it has only made a pretty noise.
picture-boy.method: Lower the bunk cord to Bo’s waiting palm
picture-boy.speech: Tests the sound of an alarm from the sleeper's position.
picture-boy.reply: I heard your bell through the floor. That means we can wake the sleeper gently.

plum-fen.want: I want the broken wheel back in time to play the small drum at supper.
plum-fen.need: Take Fen’s drumstick while the wheel comes off
plum-fen.belief: A cart and a drum can lose their beat for the same loose spoke.
plum-fen.method: Tap Fen’s spare rim for the dull note
plum-fen.speech: Sets the beat down to put a hand under a wheel.
plum-fen.reply: A wheel rolls best to a drummer who has a free hand to catch it.

plum-tallowheel.want: I want to hear my child's first drum solo without having to shout the count for them.
plum-tallowheel.belief: A child can keep time before an adult gives the beat a name.
plum-tallowheel.method: Set the smallest drum where the child can reach it
plum-tallowheel.speech: Calls his own supper the last orchard delivery.
plum-tallowheel.reply: That last basket was my supper. I always call it the delivery so nobody insists on paying.

plum-pia.want: I want the audience to wait for one plum to fall of its own accord.
plum-pia.need: Stand with Pia through one empty bar
plum-pia.belief: A long wait can change a performance more than a new note.
plum-pia.method: Mark where Pia’s first plum actually lands
plum-pia.speech: Lets a whole musical bar pass before answering.
plum-pia.reply: I thought the bar was empty until someone in the stalls took a breath.

otla-rusk.want: I want to sit down to my own supper while somebody else runs the shadow curtain.
otla-rusk.need: Take Otla’s cue from the soup spoon
otla-rusk.belief: The guest who stirs the pot sees a different show from the guest at the table.
otla-rusk.method: Hold the curtain over Otla’s warming pan
otla-rusk.speech: Taps out a kitchen cue before calling it a cue.
otla-rusk.reply: An old cook kept the beat. First time in weeks my hands got to enjoy the song.

clearance-reader-tavi.want: I would like the low-rail reading to be on the slip before someone lifts the case.
clearance-reader-tavi.need: Take Tavi’s reading from a seated position
clearance-reader-tavi.belief: The upper edge can hide a mark that is plain at a child's height.
clearance-reader-tavi.method: Tilt the Cold Store slip towards Tavi’s knee
clearance-reader-tavi.speech: Reads metal from a chair and says when it dazzles.
clearance-reader-tavi.reply: At chair height the brass shines straight into my eyes. Nobody wrote that down.

clearance-reader-jase.want: I want the wide rail to keep one handspan free for the neighbour who needs both hands.
clearance-reader-jase.need: Move Jase’s spare case back one place
clearance-reader-jase.belief: A broad shelf can become a narrow passage by lunchtime.
clearance-reader-jase.method: Walk Jase’s rail carrying a full-width tray
clearance-reader-jase.speech: Speaks of the extra handspan around a heavy case.
clearance-reader-jase.reply: That step back gave the young porter a turn to catch the heel of the case.

peg-reader-irven.want: I want the fish seller to see which old name makes the right turn at Seagrass Steps.
peg-reader-irven.need: Take Irven’s market chair for a tide
peg-reader-irven.belief: A place name has to work for someone carrying something heavy.
peg-reader-irven.method: Try Irven’s turn with the market basket
peg-reader-irven.speech: Asks for a chair in the vocabulary of a tide.
peg-reader-irven.reply: I ate sitting up. Those are two different achievements on a market day.

peg-receiver-mireth.want: I need to open the dock roll in rain without making the first date disappear.
peg-receiver-mireth.need: Keep Mireth’s spare sleeve dry under the table
peg-receiver-mireth.belief: The first drop lands where a hand has already worn the wax thin.
peg-receiver-mireth.method: Turn Mireth’s cover so rain runs off the fold
peg-receiver-mireth.speech: Finds a dry sleeve for someone before the drum starts.
peg-receiver-mireth.reply: I put the dry sleeve over her arm before the drum began. You should have seen her bow.

label-loft-keeper.want: I want the return copy to show the dock as a pilot saw it at low tide.
label-loft-keeper.need: Let Nellin’s second sheet stay beside the clean copy
label-loft-keeper.belief: A clean copy at high water can hide the reason for a rough line.
label-loft-keeper.method: Slide Nellin’s low-water edge into the dock mount
label-loft-keeper.speech: Speaks more freely beside a scratched preliminary copy.
label-loft-keeper.reply: I can point to the word we argued about. Arguing with the paper is rather easier now.

specimen-work-vera.want: I want a new clerk to hear the practice balance before a buyer is watching.
specimen-work-vera.need: Give Vera one unhurried rehearsal shift
specimen-work-vera.belief: The first sound a trainee hears in public is usually the queue.
specimen-work-vera.method: Set a harmless practice weight on Vera’s pan
specimen-work-vera.speech: Measures generosity by the length of an unhurried rehearsal.
specimen-work-vera.reply: We had time to miss a cue on purpose. The sky stayed up.

specimen-work-sali.want: I want the family who lent us water to see what happened to every cup.
specimen-work-sali.need: Reserve a cup for Sali’s returning lender
specimen-work-sali.belief: A water trial can spend the thing a family came to collect.
specimen-work-sali.method: Count the water in Sali’s two return vessels
specimen-work-sali.speech: Saves the lender a cup with their name unspoken.
specimen-work-sali.reply: She came back for the cup. The loan was the third thing we talked about.

specimen-work-tobin.want: I want the prop label to say which marks came from last night's show.
specimen-work-tobin.need: Leave Tobin’s rehearsal scratches on the spare prop
specimen-work-tobin.belief: A convincing prop can acquire a history in a single performance.
specimen-work-tobin.method: Turn the prop’s worn face towards Tobin’s stage light
specimen-work-tobin.speech: Invites the next performer to trace the old scratch first.
specimen-work-tobin.reply: He found his first scratch and put a second right beside it. That prop has learnt the part.

polar-keeper-anwen.want: I want the cold case opened without tearing the paper that has stuck to its lid.
polar-keeper-anwen.need: Keep Anwen’s readers back for one thaw
polar-keeper-anwen.belief: A good opening leaves evidence of what held the lid shut.
polar-keeper-anwen.method: Ease the tissue from Anwen’s case with the support still under it
polar-keeper-anwen.speech: Lets the temperature answer before inviting the next reader.
polar-keeper-anwen.reply: The thaw made the little blank oval darker. Nobody's thumb was anywhere near it.

polar-runner-quillan.want: I'd like a visitor to try the route to the Polar Store with my full practice load.
polar-runner-quillan.need: Take Quillan’s second trip after the shift changes
polar-runner-quillan.belief: A route tested empty says little about a carrier halfway there.
polar-runner-quillan.method: Swap the trial crate onto Quillan’s broad strap
polar-runner-quillan.speech: Starts the account again with the afternoon runner.
polar-runner-quillan.reply: The afternoon runner ties the sack upside down. Same route, different evidence.

polar-reader-orsa.want: I would like the person who sends the crate to meet the one who signs for it wet.
polar-reader-orsa.need: Leave Orsa’s arrival slip beside the dispatch slip
polar-reader-orsa.belief: An intact seal and a dry parcel are two different promises.
polar-reader-orsa.speech: Never says a departure and an arrival in the same breath.
polar-reader-orsa.reply: Departure says yes. Arrival still says perhaps. I can live with both slips on the nail.

fern-record-nemi.want: I want somebody to look at the fern’s underside before they copy my careful label.
fern-record-nemi.need: Leave Nemi’s leaf turned up for the next reader
fern-record-nemi.belief: One fern can give two views without growing another frond.
fern-record-nemi.method: Lift Nemi’s tracing from its paper hinge
fern-record-nemi.speech: Invites the next reader to turn the leaf over.
fern-record-nemi.reply: My neighbour read the underside first. He's already changed what he thinks the stain is.

fern-record-lio.want: I want the bridge crew to hear the practice call from down here on the low rail.
fern-record-lio.need: Hold Lio’s place beneath the bridge while the crew rings
fern-record-lio.belief: An instruction can cross a bridge without reaching the person under it.
fern-record-lio.method: Tap Lio’s rail below the top beam
fern-record-lio.speech: Hears the bridge signal as someone standing underneath would.
fern-record-lio.reply: Below the bridge the bell seems to come from the water. I finally understand the delay.

lantern-weave-nell.want: I want a visitor in the daylight queue to notice a mark before the sun takes it.
lantern-weave-nell.need: Stay with Nell through a change of light
lantern-weave-nell.belief: A picture has visiting hours even when the door stays open.
lantern-weave-nell.method: Angle Nell’s daylight card towards the last person in line
lantern-weave-nell.speech: Waits until the light changes before naming a colour.
lantern-weave-nell.reply: There's the second colour. All my impatient visitors went home with the first.

lantern-weave-hem.want: Give me enough shade for a reader to see where the source sheet ends.
lantern-weave-hem.need: Let Hem leave the old source drawer open
lantern-weave-hem.belief: A source laid flat over its neighbour can make one look like part of the other.
lantern-weave-hem.method: Slide Hem’s shade over the seam between the leaves
lantern-weave-hem.speech: Opens a drawer to let its smell jog a printer's memory.
lantern-weave-hem.reply: The old drawer still smells of glue. That helped our returning printer place the year.

register-reader-eneth.want: I want the first pilot off the boat to find a source that somebody can still name.
register-reader-eneth.need: Keep a chalk space for Eneth’s returning pilot
register-reader-eneth.belief: A porch open to all boats needs more than one name for a landing.
register-reader-eneth.method: Put the porch chart beside Eneth’s pilot slate
register-reader-eneth.speech: Leaves a pilot room to draw a fresh mark in chalk.
register-reader-eneth.reply: She drew in a rock nobody remembered losing. Tomorrow we'll go out and look.

register-runner-caren.want: I would like the tide date on my roll to reach the quay before the wet ink smears.
register-runner-caren.need: Take Caren’s roll by the two dry ends
register-runner-caren.belief: A dated map can lose its most important figure to a thumb.
register-runner-caren.method: Wind Caren’s dock roll around the clean peg
register-runner-caren.speech: Addresses the two dry ends of a rolled sheet separately.
register-runner-caren.reply: Two dry hands at the ends. At last I can show you the middle without flattening it.

register-clerk-elwen.want: I want each sample back in the tray a neighbour actually handled.
register-clerk-elwen.need: Leave a space for Elwen’s disputed return
register-clerk-elwen.belief: A label on a loose tray tends to follow the tray when people swap jobs.
register-clerk-elwen.method: Set Elwen’s empty tray beneath the handover slip
register-clerk-elwen.speech: Gives a disputed return a place to be answered.
register-clerk-elwen.reply: I'd hated seeing a blank beside my name. Today someone wrote a question there.

passage-halen.want: I want the ferry signal readable from the waiting line along the shoal rail.
passage-halen.need: Walk the back of Halen’s queue at low light
passage-halen.belief: A signal repeated by a stranger can change before it reaches the quay.
passage-halen.method: Hang Halen’s second flag at the lower rail
passage-halen.speech: Directs a night queue from where the last person can see.
passage-halen.reply: From the back of the queue our neat arrows point at somebody's coat.

passage-clio.want: I want the reference band to open flat without breaking the binder’s old signature.
passage-clio.need: Give Clio time to loosen one stitch
passage-clio.belief: What a binding covers can matter as much as what its pages show.
passage-clio.method: Hold Clio’s reference band at the thread hole
passage-clio.speech: Counts stitches softly back from a tight binding.
passage-clio.reply: One stitch! Underneath was the end of the word I'd been too frightened to look for.

window-guide-talden.want: I want this harbour window fitted so the late crew can set its own sightline.
window-guide-talden.need: Take Talden’s place before tightening the last screw
window-guide-talden.belief: A window fitted for the fitter can exclude the person who uses it.
window-guide-talden.method: Turn Talden’s test shutter from the visitor’s mark
window-guide-talden.speech: Changes the listener's hand position before asking about a screw.
window-guide-talden.reply: You could feel the screw tug sideways. With this hand on the rail it finally makes sense.

window-recorder-cado.want: I want a station entry that leaves room for what lay outside the frame.
window-recorder-cado.need: Keep Cado’s second viewing mark on the floor
window-recorder-cado.belief: A witness can report everything they saw and still leave out half a harbour.
window-recorder-cado.method: Align Cado’s record with the outer sill
window-recorder-cado.speech: Gives two watchers separate marks to stand on.
window-recorder-cado.reply: Two watchers now have a place to put their feet. Their sketches still differ.

reading-works-vara.want: I'd like the pilot to set a real parcel on my model landing.
reading-works-vara.need: Lend Vara one working load after the demonstration
reading-works-vara.belief: A model can succeed because the person testing it knows its trick.
reading-works-vara.method: Move Vara’s landing marker under load
reading-works-vara.speech: Waits for the working load before describing the joint.
reading-works-vara.reply: It holds at the demonstration weight. At working weight it whispers first.

reading-works-kori.want: I want the packing crew to say when the proof changed hands, even on a quiet day.
reading-works-kori.need: Keep Kori’s first return box open for the proof reader
reading-works-kori.belief: A return journey needs its own reader when a crate has been opened.
reading-works-kori.method: Compare the edge marks on Kori’s two box slips
reading-works-kori.speech: Hears the returning reader out before shutting a box.
reading-works-kori.reply: The reader found the dropped line while the sender was still at the hatch.

story-frame-keeper.want: I want my shortest caption to keep the actor who made the gesture in the story.
story-frame-keeper.need: Listen to Oriel’s long version before cutting the line
story-frame-keeper.belief: A shortened caption can accidentally make a witness the author.
story-frame-keeper.method: Read Oriel’s caption back from the theatre doorway
story-frame-keeper.speech: Calls the first cut in a long account by a relative's name.
story-frame-keeper.reply: You heard my uncle in the long one. He always was the first thing an editor cut.

number-leaf-lella.want: I want a first-time runner to make the turn without having to look up at me.
number-leaf-lella.need: Ask Lella’s trainee to lead the way back
number-leaf-lella.belief: A guide has succeeded when the learner can turn around and guide them.
number-leaf-lella.method: Carry the low practice board at the trainee’s height
number-leaf-lella.speech: Follows a trainee's route without calling out the next turn.
number-leaf-lella.reply: She took a different alley back. Next time she's going to teach the outward walk too.

number-leaf-omrin.want: I want the correction to be as easy to find as my original finding.
number-leaf-omrin.need: Let Omrin keep the old wording in reach
number-leaf-omrin.belief: A correction hidden in a better drawer can still fail its first reader.
number-leaf-omrin.method: Tie Omrin’s correction card to the first catalogue peg
number-leaf-omrin.speech: Keeps the old phrase close while reading the revision.
number-leaf-omrin.reply: I don't have to defend that old phrase to let somebody see what got changed.

depot-keeper-eland.want: I want every tool on loan to come home with the condition in which it worked.
depot-keeper-eland.need: Leave Eland’s loan label room for a failed trial
depot-keeper-eland.belief: A depot lends a method with an instrument, whether it remembers to say so or not.
depot-keeper-eland.method: Try the returning gauge against Eland’s depot mark
depot-keeper-eland.speech: Praises a failed test that comes back with its borrowed equipment.
depot-keeper-eland.reply: A line for the failed trial! Our borrowers may finally believe they can bring things back.

depot-visitor-mayle.want: I'd like to see the curtain from my mother's seat this time.
depot-visitor-mayle.need: Take Mayle’s porter strap at the end of rehearsal
depot-visitor-mayle.belief: What a cloth shows depends on who gets the evening off to see it.
depot-visitor-mayle.method: Lift the borrowed frame onto Mayle’s depot stand
depot-visitor-mayle.speech: Measures rehearsal by the mark a strap leaves on a porter.
depot-visitor-mayle.reply: The porter strap leaves a purple stripe. Odd what a rehearsal leaves off its report.

reference-line-deva.want: I want the pattern shop to show the small difference that kept one apprentice's work from fitting.
reference-line-deva.need: Keep Deva’s rejected pattern out of the scrap bin
reference-line-deva.belief: A close fit can teach more than a perfect fit if the trace is left visible.
reference-line-deva.method: Set the two pattern edges on Deva’s light board
reference-line-deva.speech: Calls the discarded pattern a thing someone can still use.
reference-line-deva.reply: A girl picked the failed pattern over the pretty one. Said she could see how it was made.

reference-line-noll.want: I want the two lanes to have the same starting load before anyone calls one faster.
reference-line-noll.need: Give Noll time to reset the short lane
reference-line-noll.belief: A shortcut can be measured fairly only if the starting line travels with it.
reference-line-noll.method: Walk Noll’s marked load from both starting pegs
reference-line-noll.speech: Takes time to see a lane from the shortest runner's height.
reference-line-noll.reply: First runner through found a shortcut. I hadn't seen the floor from down there.

object-use-aven.want: I want a loft hand on the ground to be able to open the crate alone.
object-use-aven.need: Take Aven’s packed crate down to the receiving bench
object-use-aven.belief: Packing is only half done until the other person can undo it.
object-use-aven.method: Test the new loop in Aven’s carrying sling
object-use-aven.speech: Judges a packing job from the receiving bench.
object-use-aven.reply: At the receiving bench the lid opens against the rail. Fine thing to find out before loading.

object-use-veya.want: I want a fair swap to leave both sides a way to check what changed hands.
object-use-veya.need: Stand in the buyer’s place at Veya’s exchange bench
object-use-veya.belief: An exchange receipt has two owners even when only one has a pen.
object-use-veya.method: Match Veya’s two halves of the tally
object-use-veya.speech: Moves to the buyer's side to talk about a visible price.
object-use-veya.reply: I can see my elbow blocks the price. I owe yesterday's buyer a word.

object-use-coru.want: I would like the join to show which piece was replaced at the bay.
object-use-coru.need: Leave Coru’s repair line uncovered for an afternoon
object-use-coru.belief: A repair can keep a tool in service without having to disappear.
object-use-coru.method: Turn Coru’s practice joint across the grain
object-use-coru.speech: Treats a seam as something visitors can read with a finger.
object-use-coru.reply: Two children traced the seam before they read the label. The repair has found an audience.

object-use-sivra.want: I want the trace on the gallery wall to keep the direction of the hand that made it.
object-use-sivra.need: Give Sivra a chance to draw from the other end
object-use-sivra.belief: A traced mark can look intentional after the hand that slipped has gone.
object-use-sivra.method: Follow Sivra’s line back to its starting burr
object-use-sivra.speech: Draws towards a familiar piling from the unfamiliar side.
object-use-sivra.reply: The pilot's end has one extra piling. My neat near view just blotted it out.

coast-olwen-veer.want: I want a practice plate that can be read when the Headland wind shakes its frame.
coast-olwen-veer.need: Stand with Olwen through a gust before marking the result
coast-olwen-veer.belief: A steady hand indoors can borrow certainty from a quiet room.
coast-olwen-veer.method: Hold Olwen’s practice plate at its loose corner
coast-olwen-veer.speech: Leaves a forecast sentence open through the next gust.
coast-olwen-veer.reply: The gust lifted a corner a second before the line moved. We have a better warning.

reference-keeper-cerin.want: I need the fitter on the second shift to find the reference stop with gloves on.
reference-keeper-cerin.need: Give Cerin the spare gloves for a blind fit
reference-keeper-cerin.belief: A correct reference point can be useless if a hand cannot locate it.
reference-keeper-cerin.method: Seat Cerin’s gauge against the worn stop
reference-keeper-cerin.speech: Puts on spare gloves to speak as the next worker.
reference-keeper-cerin.reply: In the gloves you feel the burr on the inside. Bare fingers slid right over it.

reference-observer-loen.want: I want the night shift to inherit the time of the change, not only the final number.
reference-observer-loen.need: Leave Loen's two shift times on the same slip
reference-observer-loen.belief: An accurate reading without its hour can belong to the wrong crew.
reference-observer-loen.method: Turn Loen’s log to the handover crease
reference-observer-loen.speech: Places the kettle's boiling between two recorded shift times.
reference-observer-loen.reply: Same slip, both times, and one kettle that boiled while we were waiting.

callboard-reader.want: I'd like to run the call with my own name on it before it is crossed off as delivered.
callboard-reader.need: Let Neris read the callboard from the stair
callboard-reader.belief: A call seen by a runner has yet to reach the person named on it.
callboard-reader.method: Take Neris’s return line up the civic steps
callboard-reader.speech: Calls a name from the stair before trusting the callboard.
callboard-reader.reply: Down the stair our evening call sounds like the end of a different name.

callboard-keeper.want: I want visitors to see exactly what I signed for, even when my name only just fits.
callboard-keeper.need: Give Orella another line beneath the visitors’ stamp
callboard-keeper.belief: A signature cannot certify the page that was under the one I saw.
callboard-keeper.method: Hold the visiting sheet clear of Orella’s lower copy
callboard-keeper.speech: Makes room for a visitor's pencil under the formal stamp.
callboard-keeper.reply: Our next visitor wrote “why?” underneath the stamp. I’ve sharpened a pencil for the answer.

second-reading-linnet.want: I want the borrowed bell back with its harbour note intact.
second-reading-linnet.need: Let Linnet ring the loan bell before the Council starts
second-reading-linnet.belief: A changed tone can carry a history that the loan docket never requested.
second-reading-linnet.method: Listen from Linnet’s old position at the end of the rail
second-reading-linnet.speech: Rings the little loan bell before the large public one.
second-reading-linnet.reply: Somebody came back with the little bell before the big hearing had even opened.

field-store-aven.want: I'd like the practice tray to spill here before a neighbour’s drinking water is in it.
field-store-aven.need: Give Aven one empty return run
field-store-aven.belief: A dry run saves water only when somebody records the spill.
field-store-aven.method: Tilt Aven’s spare tray over the common basin
field-store-aven.speech: Listens for the rattle on the empty return.
field-store-aven.reply: An empty run rattles in a different place. My first delivery of the day is to the fitter.

store-odal.want: I want the cloth sample judged after someone has folded and unfolded it.
store-odal.need: Leave Odal’s crease on the handling sample
store-odal.belief: A fabric keeps a visitor's touch longer than it keeps the shop light.
store-odal.method: Fold Odal’s test strip against the original seam
store-odal.speech: Uses a borrower's crease as the start of a handling direction.
store-odal.reply: The crease leads right to the thumb. I let the next borrower start from that end.

store-osma.want: I'd like the two bearings read at the same bell before the watchers argue about the ship.
store-osma.need: Wait beside Osma for the next shared signal
store-osma.belief: Two honest bearings can put a moving boat in a place it never reached.
store-osma.method: Turn Osma’s paired sight cards towards the bell
store-osma.speech: Waits for both shifts to finish signalling before claiming a job.
store-osma.reply: After the two signals there's a moment where neither shift owns the job. I stayed for it.

store-taev.want: I want the stores docket to show which parcel had already been opened.
store-taev.need: Keep Taev’s torn packing band beside the seal
store-taev.belief: A full inventory can hide an interruption between two signatures.
store-taev.method: Match Taev’s cut band to the receiving notch
store-taev.speech: Keeps a torn band in the story after the package is resealed.
store-taev.reply: That band tore before the stamp was set. The parcel has had a longer day than we thought.

store-zyra.want: I want my surface copy to show the place where the original turns away from the light.
store-zyra.need: Let Zyra change the rake of the lamp
store-zyra.belief: A flat copy asks its reader to imagine depth it can no longer show.
store-zyra.method: Tip Zyra’s rubbing across the raised edge
store-zyra.speech: Changes a lamp angle before giving a second description.
store-zyra.reply: A low light makes yesterday's groove pop right out. My hand fits it.

glass-keeper.want: I want the hinge to yield to a visitor with only one hand free.
glass-keeper.need: Try Quena’s mount with the other hand occupied
glass-keeper.belief: A latch is part of what an exhibit lets a visitor know.
glass-keeper.method: Lift Quena’s practice lid from the lower grip
glass-keeper.speech: Addresses the one free thumb on a loaded carrier.
glass-keeper.reply: One arm full, one thumb free. I can turn the mount without dropping my lunch.

glass-rail-reader.want: I want the reading between my rounds to count even if I never make it to the front rail.
glass-rail-reader.need: Hold Osyth’s carrier cart for one page
glass-rail-reader.belief: A hurried reader deserves a way to get back to the same sentence.
glass-rail-reader.method: Mark Osyth’s sightline from the broad rail
glass-rail-reader.speech: Talks in borrowed intervals of a porter's reading time.
glass-rail-reader.reply: I read a whole page without checking the wheel. I'd forgotten what the writer was saying.

glass-pocket-reader.want: I'd like the little desk by the coats to have a lamp of its own.
glass-pocket-reader.need: Keep Rennel’s last chair free when the hooks fill up
glass-pocket-reader.belief: A small desk can admit a reader the grand room turns away.
glass-pocket-reader.method: Try the coat-hook label under Rennel’s reading lamp
glass-pocket-reader.speech: Reserves the closing line for the crew who arrive after the hooks fill.
glass-pocket-reader.reply: Late crew sat together for once. They have an entirely different name for that cue.

shore-reply-velna.want: I want the outgoing register to say which flag the boat could actually see.
shore-reply-velna.need: Ask Velna’s far watcher to call it back
shore-reply-velna.belief: Sending a signal and receiving a signal are two different events in my book.
shore-reply-velna.method: Read the reflected flag from Velna’s shed window
shore-reply-velna.speech: Repeats the word the far watcher actually heard.
shore-reply-velna.reply: The far watcher called my half-heard word back correctly. It was the gesture she missed.

shore-reply-miri.want: I want to give my own first reading before anyone tells me what Velna meant.
shore-reply-miri.need: Keep the signal key closed while Miri answers
shore-reply-miri.belief: Agreement after seeing the key says less about what reached me.
shore-reply-miri.method: Hold up Miri’s return flag before comparing slips
shore-reply-miri.speech: Lets a reply from memory precede the signal key.
shore-reply-miri.reply: I answered without the key. My reply was a street name I'd never seen written down.

ferry-window-nessa.want: I'd like the ferry model to teach the turn even when I step out of the room.
ferry-window-nessa.need: Give Nessa’s apprentice the model tiller
ferry-window-nessa.belief: A model route deserves a trial by someone who did not build the bank.
ferry-window-nessa.method: Move Nessa’s practice boat in from the other approach
ferry-window-nessa.speech: Passes the model tiller to a learner before naming the current.
ferry-window-nessa.reply: Our new pilot let go as the model turned. Turns out the tiller pulls left on its own.

ferry-window-merrit.want: I would like to take the second approach without my teacher moving my wrist.
ferry-window-merrit.need: Let Merrit make one slow turn unaided
ferry-window-merrit.belief: If a guiding hand makes the turn I still have to learn it myself.
ferry-window-merrit.method: Take the passenger seat in Merrit’s practice skiff
ferry-window-merrit.speech: Counts an unaided half-turn as a victory worth describing.
ferry-window-merrit.reply: Slowly round, all by myself. I'd take that one turn over a whole lap of applause.

oracle-keeper.want: I want the apprentice printer to know what the old press used to do before we mend it.
oracle-keeper.need: Set aside Nerin’s last flawed impression
oracle-keeper.belief: A fault that is removed without a sample can be blamed on the last worker.
oracle-keeper.method: Take a dry pull from Nerin’s loose plate
oracle-keeper.speech: Reads improvement from the first imperfect impression.
oracle-keeper.reply: You can see which corner I fixed. The clean sheet never could tell that part.

oracle-reader.want: I want the maintenance crew sent to the loose hinge before the next bell.
oracle-reader.need: Give Thessa a route that includes the last return
oracle-reader.belief: A short route can leave a long queue at the one stop it skips.
oracle-reader.method: Walk Thessa’s repair order in reverse
oracle-reader.speech: Keeps the homebound porter in a route description.
oracle-reader.reply: We met our own carrier coming home. He was holding a tool nobody had logged going out.

badge-keeper.want: I want the name beside a badge to lead back to something a worker can still show.
badge-keeper.need: Let Brenna’s quieter apprentice tell the story first
badge-keeper.belief: A badge that remembers only a name has lost most of its work.
badge-keeper.method: Find the working sample behind Brenna’s ribbon
badge-keeper.speech: Asks the quieter worker to begin the story before the supervisor.
badge-keeper.reply: Her version starts three hours earlier. I'd only seen the job once it came past my bench.

schedule-eome.want: I'd like the cloth room to return the lender's fold as carefully as its colour.
schedule-eome.need: Leave Eome space for the old fold in the new mount
schedule-eome.belief: A fold can be evidence of use even when it looks untidy on a wall.
schedule-eome.method: Turn Eome’s cloth under the shaded pane
schedule-eome.speech: Uses an old fold to recognise a lender's way of holding cloth.
schedule-eome.reply: The lender ran her finger straight to the fold. She knew it before she saw the colour.

schedule-enel.want: My favourite jug has a chip exactly where my brother used to put his thumb. The stand hides it.
schedule-enel.need: Let Enel choose which side of the jug faces out
schedule-enel.belief: Somebody held this before somebody collected it.
schedule-enel.method: Fit a felt wedge beneath Enel’s jug
schedule-enel.speech: Places the remembered thumb against a chipped rim.
schedule-enel.reply: There. That's where his thumb went. I'd forgotten how small a mark it was.

schedule-karth.want: The wheel that sticks is the only one my boy can take apart by himself.
schedule-karth.need: Set aside a sticking wheel for the young fitter
schedule-karth.belief: A machine that misbehaves can show a learner where to start.
schedule-karth.method: Turn Karth’s axle with the casing open
schedule-karth.speech: Calls a sticking wheel a beginning for a young fitter.
schedule-karth.reply: He asked for a second look at the stiff wheel. Last week he wouldn't touch it.

schedule-veira.want: I'd like to print the smudged sheet. That's where my mother tried three words for home.
schedule-veira.need: Give the printer a space for the rubbed-out words
schedule-veira.belief: An early word can let us hear someone looking for the later one.
schedule-veira.method: Ink Veira’s proof from the softer side
schedule-veira.speech: Reads erased words aloud before the clean word for home.
schedule-veira.reply: Mother read all three words and chose a fourth. Still room on the proof.

jig-shop-nesta.want: Somebody tell the apprentice her thumb found the wobble before my jig did.
jig-shop-nesta.need: Put the apprentice’s chalk mark beside the shop stamp
jig-shop-nesta.belief: A fit has to hold for the hand that will actually use it.
jig-shop-nesta.method: Pass Nesta’s joint to the smallest hand on shift
jig-shop-nesta.speech: Praises a thumb's discovery before the stamp on a jig.
jig-shop-nesta.reply: The girl signed the chalk mark. Her handwriting wobbled just as much as my first jig.

curtain-ethren.want: I practised the call at breakfast. Our kettle answered before anybody else did.
curtain-ethren.need: Give Ethren one quiet run before the bells
curtain-ethren.belief: If a crew hears two different orders, the louder voice hasn't settled it.
curtain-ethren.method: Walk the length of Ethren’s call carrying an empty tray
curtain-ethren.speech: Hears the kettle as an unusually prompt member of a crew.
curtain-ethren.reply: I heard the end of my own call. In a crowd I never knew I'd been swallowing it.

memory-cart-edrin.want: My old cart left a rut right there. The new rail sends strangers into it.
memory-cart-edrin.need: Keep the turn clear while Edrin finds the old wheel track
memory-cart-edrin.belief: Feet remember a load differently from an empty pavement.
memory-cart-edrin.method: Push the borrowed cart round Edrin’s outside turn
memory-cart-edrin.speech: Recalls a bend by the weight once on the cart.
memory-cart-edrin.reply: Two tracks, one wheel. It got round because the carter leaned out there.

memory-cart-nella.want: I wear out my left boot first. Nobody who traces my route on paper guesses why.
memory-cart-nella.need: Walk alongside Nella at her own pace
memory-cart-nella.belief: A path drawn straight can cost someone a second journey.
memory-cart-nella.method: Trade places at the rail where Nella changes sides
memory-cart-nella.speech: Makes the wear on a boot part of a route description.
memory-cart-nella.reply: You slowed at the puddle before I said a word. My left boot thanks you.

dispatch-stats-orla.want: My sister's letters all came down the freight rail. I learned to hear her paper arrive.
dispatch-stats-orla.need: Keep the dispatch slot free for one thin envelope
dispatch-stats-orla.belief: A wrong tray can deliver joy and still need fixing.
dispatch-stats-orla.method: Run Orla’s empty envelope down both dispatch rails
dispatch-stats-orla.speech: Hears an envelope slap before asking who sent it.
dispatch-stats-orla.reply: There it is. Hear that little slap? I could sort her letter with my eyes shut.

price-drawers-sella.want: The papers in my left pocket promise supper. I'm still waiting on the ones in my right.
price-drawers-sella.need: Hold a place at Sella’s table until the delivery comes
price-drawers-sella.belief: A promise and a meal weigh differently to the person waiting.
price-drawers-sella.method: Pin the actual delivery slip outside Sella’s pocket
price-drawers-sella.speech: Moves between promises and meals by way of two real pockets.
price-drawers-sella.reply: We shared the last potato. That was worth eight entries in my promise book.

script-irwen.want: I lost my voice on the last verse. A girl in the back finished it in a tune I didn't know.
script-irwen.need: Let the girl give Irwen the tune before the next reading
script-irwen.belief: A verse belongs a little to the person who brings it safely home.
script-irwen.method: Tap the rest where Irwen stopped singing
script-irwen.speech: Leaves the last note available to a singer at the back.
script-irwen.reply: She taught me the bit her mother hums while onions brown. It belongs in the reading now.

script-rennick.want: My daughter asked which side of a stage door counts as the theatre. I owe her a better answer.
script-rennick.need: Leave Rennick’s daughter a seat on the working side
script-rennick.belief: The people who hear the show through a door get a different show.
script-rennick.method: Ease Rennick’s door until the same line carries both ways
script-rennick.speech: Speaks from the working side of a stage door.
script-rennick.reply: She counted eleven people working through the scene. Two actors on the other side.

script-cetra.want: I can do my teacher's voice so well that sometimes the little ones ask when I'm coming on.
script-cetra.need: Save Cetra a turn in her own speaking voice
script-cetra.belief: Lending somebody your voice is a choice you get to take back.
script-cetra.method: Draw the curtain between Cetra’s two tellings
script-cetra.speech: Switches out of a borrowed voice for a childhood story.
script-cetra.reply: I told them about losing a tooth. They all wanted the next bit in that voice.

script-talven.want: My best friend liked the ending we cut. He's the only person I can't face at the edition desk.
script-talven.need: Make two spaces at the desk for Talven and his friend
script-talven.belief: An earlier ending can outlive the page we give to the printer.
script-talven.method: Turn Talven’s folded proof to the cut ending
script-talven.speech: Invites an unhappy reader to take the other chair at the desk.
script-talven.reply: My friend still wants the old ending. He lent me a pencil all the same.

correspondence-mera.want: The first letter I ever sent came back with a red thumb on it. I still wonder whose.
correspondence-mera.need: Give Mera a minute to write the return address in full
correspondence-mera.belief: A letter should be able to find the hand that sent it.
correspondence-mera.method: Lay Mera’s finished envelopes with their backs showing
correspondence-mera.speech: Follows the print of a red thumb backward along a delivery.
correspondence-mera.reply: The runner could actually find me to ask about the red print. That changes our ending.

correspondence-ansel.want: Two names come out alike when the floor is busy. Yesterday I answered for a man I'd never met.
correspondence-ansel.need: Keep a finger on each name until both runners answer
correspondence-ansel.belief: A handoff is a meeting, even when the names sound the same.
correspondence-ansel.method: Read Ansel’s two receipts back to their separate bearers
correspondence-ansel.speech: Waits for both bearers of a similar name to answer.
correspondence-ansel.reply: Each one answered. Their voices sound nothing alike once you let them speak.

forest-hook-sorell.want: I want that muddy bootmark on the slate for another day. It's my father's first walk since winter.
forest-hook-sorell.need: Save Sorell a corner for the print before the slate is wiped
forest-hook-sorell.belief: An ordinary trail mark can matter long after the trail dries.
forest-hook-sorell.method: Trace around Sorell’s wet heel mark with a stick of chalk
forest-hook-sorell.speech: Gives a bootprint a whole afternoon on the public slate.
forest-hook-sorell.reply: The print is safe round the edge. Father drew his walking stick beside it.

shutter-ilin.want: I know which shutter squeaks. The girl who oils them knows which one never opens.
shutter-ilin.need: Take Ilin on the oiling round before the visitors arrive
shutter-ilin.belief: Silence can mean a hinge works or that nobody gets to use it.
