shutter-ilin.method: Unhook Ilin’s silent shutter from the yard side
shutter-ilin.speech: Listens to the hinge that never needs oil.
shutter-ilin.reply: That shutter hasn't been opened for a season. Somebody had painted the catch shut.

shutter-tavin.want: They remember the parcel that fell. I'd like them to remember the runner who caught it.
shutter-tavin.need: Set Tavin’s tray down beside the runner’s bench
shutter-tavin.belief: A safe arrival can hide a very narrow escape.
shutter-tavin.method: Balance Tavin’s empty tray where the parcel slipped
shutter-tavin.speech: Names the person who caught a parcel before the person who dropped it.
shutter-tavin.reply: The catcher came to sit beside me. I've learnt the name I should've shouted.

shutter-merra.want: I copied the letter in a fine clear hand. My aunt says it doesn't sound like her any more.
shutter-merra.need: Give the aunt a quiet turn to read Merra’s copy aloud
shutter-merra.belief: A pause can travel in a voice and go missing in a tidy copy.
shutter-merra.method: Tap Merra’s desk at the aunt’s original line breaks
shutter-merra.speech: Restores an aunt's pauses to the sound of a clean copy.
shutter-merra.reply: Auntie put all the stops back as she read. Listen to the air after the last word.

open-place-blythe.want: I took the long steps so the copy would stay dry. Now the docket calls me late.
open-place-blythe.need: Wait with Blythe for the porter who saw the rain
open-place-blythe.belief: Arrival time alone won't tell you which thing the runner saved.
open-place-blythe.method: Spread Blythe’s dry sheet next to the wet wrapping
open-place-blythe.speech: Tells the long walk by its dry envelope.
open-place-blythe.reply: The porter knew how hard it rained. The docket now has a damp thumb beside the time.

open-place-ione.want: My grandson thinks carrying the canal key means I own the water. He's saving for his own.
open-place-ione.need: Leave Ione time to show him the people waiting at both gates
open-place-ione.belief: The hand with the key borrows other people's trust.
open-place-ione.method: Turn Ione’s key from the bank where the queue begins
open-place-ione.speech: Explains a key by counting the queues on both banks.
open-place-ione.reply: He saw both queues. This afternoon he's making keys out of twigs for everyone.

open-place-edvin.want: I set out four chairs. The fifth witness saw me count them and went home.
open-place-edvin.need: Keep a place at Edvin’s desk for a witness returning late
open-place-edvin.belief: A hearing can lose a voice before its first word.
open-place-edvin.method: Carry Edvin’s spare chair through the public door
open-place-edvin.speech: Counts the chair nobody set out when naming the witnesses.
open-place-edvin.reply: The fifth witness came through the door twice. The second time she stayed.

facing-sella.want: One empty hook means a missing coat. The other means a child finally got a part.
facing-sella.need: Let Sella keep the two empty hooks apart
facing-sella.belief: An absence needs a story before it can stand for anything.
facing-sella.method: Hang Sella’s rehearsal tags underneath the bare hooks
facing-sella.speech: Lets two empty hooks tell different backstage stories.
facing-sella.reply: One hook is a worry and one is an opening night. Nice to see them finally get their labels.

auda-wick.want: My bell can be heard on both banks. The letter in my pocket changes what it means on just one.
auda-wick.need: Cover the bell rope while Auda crosses with the letter
auda-wick.belief: Hearing a signal and knowing what to do may happen on different days.
auda-wick.method: Ring Auda’s small handbell from the far bank
auda-wick.speech: Lets a letter change the meaning of the bell she rings.
auda-wick.reply: I got back in time to hear my own bell from the steps. I've delivered both halves now.

noll-wick.want: I used to fill every gap on the landing. Last night someone sang my rest back to me.
noll-wick.need: Stand beside Noll through the quiet bar
noll-wick.belief: A rest belongs to whoever dares come in after it.
noll-wick.method: Draw Noll’s silent bow through one whole turn
noll-wick.speech: Leaves a gap another player can sing across.
noll-wick.reply: Your empty hands stayed up. The girl who sang the rest thought you were conducting.

ket-ribble.want: At my table the loaf comes round twice. There's a boy who only ever takes the second offer.
ket-ribble.need: Save Ket’s last heel for the second round
ket-ribble.belief: A person can be hungry while the first plate passes untouched.
ket-ribble.method: Carry Ket’s bread past the door a second time
ket-ribble.speech: Makes the second offer sound as ordinary as the first.
ket-ribble.reply: Second round. He took the heel and gave me his opinion of the crust.

fen-clove.want: I tell the night story from memory because the scale master's handwriting still frightens me.
fen-clove.need: Sit with Fen while the old scale book is open
fen-clove.belief: Telling it aloud lets me hear where I borrow somebody else's certainty.
fen-clove.method: Let Fen weigh the counterweight before weighing a tale
fen-clove.speech: Tests an inherited ledger against the sound of a spoken tale.
fen-clove.reply: That old book has soup on the corner. My master used to eat over it too.

register-tovrie.want: The warm print fades faster in company. I wanted to show it to a person who travels slowly.
register-tovrie.need: Keep the warm tile beside the late visitor’s seat
register-tovrie.belief: A trace can last long enough for one witness and vanish before another.
register-tovrie.method: Shield Tovrie’s marked tile with an upturned cup
register-tovrie.speech: Follows a fading print at the speed of the slowest visitor.
register-tovrie.reply: The print stayed warm until she reached us. She said it looked very like a shy moon.

register-orren-bell.want: Between the flash and the bell I always count my little brother in. He knows by now.
register-orren-bell.need: Count the quiet beats with Orren at the far rail
register-orren-bell.belief: Sharing a signal means finding out when the last person receives it.
register-orren-bell.method: Lift Orren’s ribbon as soon as the light arrives
register-orren-bell.speech: Counts quiet beats in a sibling's familiar rhythm.
register-orren-bell.reply: Three to the rail. Four to the sheds. My brother's got a job counting with me now.

register-vellune.want: Everyone draws the front of my nest. I was a chick once. I remember the way out.
register-vellune.need: Leave the back opening clear while Vellune watches
register-vellune.belief: Shelter has to give its occupant a way to leave.
register-vellune.method: Turn Vellune’s little nest so its two doors show
register-vellune.speech: Offers a sheltered listener a clear way back out.
register-vellune.reply: The smallest bird used the back door twice. Never even looked at the front.

register-bayette.want: My father carved his initial backwards. Copies get it right more often than he did.
register-bayette.need: Save Bayette the first crooked impression
register-bayette.belief: A beautifully corrected mark can lose the hand that made it.
register-bayette.method: Press Bayette’s stamp into a scrap facing away from the mirror
register-bayette.speech: Cherishes the backward letter in a family stamp.
register-bayette.reply: Dad laughed. Said at last I'd got his mistake exactly right.

register-ostel.want: I lent them my horizon. They sent it back with the fishing huts rubbed off.
register-ostel.need: Keep Ostel’s hut on the returned strip
register-ostel.belief: A straight line on a chart may cross somebody's front step.
register-ostel.method: Lift Ostel’s skyline strip against the harbour window
register-ostel.speech: Brings a fishing roof back into the straight skyline.
register-ostel.reply: That's the roof of our old net shed. Neat skyline, terrible place for a straight line.

register-brannic.want: I clap from behind the door for the stagehands. The leading player thinks I'm his aunt.
register-brannic.need: Hold the stage door for Brannic until the hands have bowed
register-brannic.belief: You cannot tell who received a thank-you by counting the noise.
register-brannic.method: Listen with Brannic on both sides of the applause
register-brannic.speech: Claps through the door for people out of sight.
register-brannic.reply: The hands bowed and the leading player clapped with me. I may have acquired a nephew.

register-sessa-vale.want: When the baskets come home empty I want to know if we sold all the fruit or never had any.
register-sessa-vale.need: Wait beside Sessa until the pickers return
register-sessa-vale.belief: The same empty basket can bring very different news to a household.
register-sessa-vale.method: Hang Sessa’s basket beside its morning loading card
register-sessa-vale.speech: Waits for the pickers to explain an empty basket.
register-sessa-vale.reply: Baskets came back empty with a sprig in each. They'd had a fine morning.

register-maro.want: I bought my sister a ribbon she could see from the lane. The bell rang and the wind took it sideways.
register-maro.need: Stand at the bend where Maro’s sister waits
register-maro.belief: A signal works for the person who can receive it from there.
register-maro.method: Carry Maro’s ribbon to the bend before pulling the cord
register-maro.speech: Reads a signal from the turn where a sister watches.
register-maro.reply: She could see it at the bend. From our end it looked as if it had hardly moved.

register-ro.want: Another window! My landlord groaned. Then he saw which child couldn't see over the sill.
register-ro.need: Keep the small visitor’s line of sight open for Ro
register-ro.belief: A view changes with the body that comes to it.
register-ro.method: Slide Ro’s little window down to the low sill
register-ro.speech: Installs a window at the height of the newest spectator.
register-ro.reply: Her very first sight was of the window cleaner. They waved solemnly at each other.

liri-pell.want: A good fitter leaves room for a glove. Nobody taught me that until winter bit my knuckle.
liri-pell.need: Let Liri try the handle in a winter glove
liri-pell.belief: The tool has to fit on the day the job is hardest.
liri-pell.method: Cover Liri’s gauge hand with the thick mitten
liri-pell.speech: Talks winter tools through a pair of gloves.
liri-pell.reply: I can get my knuckles round it now. Winter's going to have to find another joke.

tessel-fen.want: I mended the ferry path so my mother could bring the wide cart. The fine new board blocks her turn.
tessel-fen.need: Give Tessel room to turn the loaded handcart
tessel-fen.belief: A board can guide the walker and bar the porter in the same breath.
tessel-fen.method: Roll Tessel’s cart around the foot of the notice
tessel-fen.speech: Describes the turning circle of the widest family cart.
tessel-fen.reply: Mother took the turn in one try. Left two magnificent wet arcs for the surveyor.

aven-dorr.want: The first order I signed was the one I'd begged my own foreperson to change. My hand remembered the position.
aven-dorr.need: Keep an apprentice’s stool at Aven’s next shift meeting
aven-dorr.belief: A signature can turn yesterday's complaint into tomorrow's instruction.
aven-dorr.method: Turn Aven’s old rota round to the apprentice’s side
aven-dorr.speech: Reads a foreperson's signature in an apprentice's voice.
aven-dorr.reply: An apprentice pointed out the longest shift on the rota. It was my own.

agate-vale.want: I repaired the grand chair. The quiet witness chose the broken one by the door.
agate-vale.need: Sit by Agate while she mends the chair the witness chose
agate-vale.belief: Comfort includes being able to leave a room with dignity.
agate-vale.method: Measure Agate’s loose chair leg on the hearing floor
agate-vale.speech: Asks which seat the witness can leave easily.
agate-vale.reply: She's taken the seat by the door again. This time she left her coat on the peg.

courier-bew.want: A crate marked light is still my back's problem if the last shipper guessed.
courier-bew.need: Give Bew time to ask the loader about the bottom crate
courier-bew.belief: Freight words are promises to the next pair of arms.
courier-bew.method: Lift one end of Bew’s crate before moving the tally
courier-bew.speech: Weighs the clerk's words in the loader's hands.
courier-bew.reply: It was the bottom plank that was heavy. The loader remembered the repair.

courier-pella.want: I can call thunder in three voices. What I want is one person to whisper when I've missed my cue.
courier-pella.need: Wait in Pella’s wing with the soft warning cue
courier-pella.belief: Making a loud room work sometimes takes a quiet correction.
courier-pella.method: Tap Pella’s prompt rail with one finger
courier-pella.speech: Listens for a soft rail tap before the loud cue.
courier-pella.reply: Your tap went straight down my shoe. I went on without having to look at the wings.

almanac-rix.want: I print invitations and drum the parade. The people who can't read my card can follow me right past their own turning.
almanac-rix.need: Hold Rix’s corner until the last guest turns
almanac-rix.belief: An invitation has to reach the person it was meant to welcome.
almanac-rix.method: Beat Rix’s turn signal from inside the side street
almanac-rix.speech: Drums directions from inside the street where a guest must turn.
almanac-rix.reply: The last guest led me back by a lane I've drummed past every spring.

almanac-jori.want: I made a lantern that paints the pavement blue. The girl upstairs only sees the unpainted side.
almanac-jori.need: Bring Jori’s lamp up to the girl’s landing
almanac-jori.belief: A picture has another audience on the other side of the glass.
almanac-jori.method: Turn Jori’s pane slowly beside the upstairs window
almanac-jori.speech: Gives a second colour from the other side of the pane.
almanac-jori.reply: Upstairs the whole lantern was the colour of a lemon. She drew her own picture.

cup-cen.want: I cut the cocoa price into the sign in winter. My wrists hurt at the thought of changing it in spring.
cup-cen.need: Cover the counter while Cen cuts a space for a loose price
cup-cen.belief: The cost of changing a sign can quietly decide what it says.
cup-cen.method: Slide a new wooden numeral into Cen’s cocoa board
cup-cen.speech: Feels a price change in the wrists of the sign cutter.
cup-cen.reply: The new price fits in the old sign. Now my hands can go back to making cocoa.

cup-kit.want: A loose cart wheel and a late actor make the very same noise behind the curtain. Never tell a fitter that.
cup-kit.need: Wait with Kit until the next sound has a face
cup-kit.belief: Knowing the cue by heart doesn't tell you what made it today.
cup-kit.method: Roll Kit’s unladen cart past the backstage cloth
cup-kit.speech: Lets a cart wheel and an actor both answer the cue.
cup-kit.reply: The sound was the young actor pushing the cart. We were both right for half a second.

stacks-opal.want: I make cabinets that travel. My father measures a good cupboard by the number of storms it stays shut.
stacks-opal.need: Give Opal and her father turns at the same latch
stacks-opal.belief: A safe latch has to open for the hand that comes after the storm.
stacks-opal.method: Tilt Opal’s sample cabinet as if the ferry were turning
stacks-opal.speech: Asks a ferry passenger to open the cabinet latch.
stacks-opal.reply: Father opened my latch smiling. I've never before seen a cupboard pass a family inspection.

stacks-tallis.want: My niece asked why the lamp always finds the hero. I used to rig the rope. I ought to answer her.
stacks-tallis.need: Keep the lamp on Tallis’s niece while she asks her question
stacks-tallis.belief: Somebody chooses the person everybody sees first.
stacks-tallis.method: Hand Tallis the side pulley for the second pool of light
stacks-tallis.speech: Gives a pool of stage light to the hand on the pulley.
stacks-tallis.reply: My niece gave her pool of light to the woman on the pulley. That's a director for you.

wire-oda.want: I have my mother's ferry song down to the last note. When she laughed the needle skipped.
wire-oda.need: Give Oda her own turn to tell what happened in the gap
wire-oda.belief: The part a recorder loses may be what a listener came to keep.
wire-oda.method: Play Oda’s silent groove at the old ferry bench
wire-oda.speech: Hears laughter in the skipped groove of a recording.
wire-oda.reply: Mother sneezed after she laughed. I had completely forgotten until you let me tell it.

wire-tavi.want: My legs have retired. My hands still jump when the receiving wheel gives its first click.
wire-tavi.need: Give Tavi the first turn at a seated height
wire-tavi.belief: A retired runner still knows what a late handoff feels like.
wire-tavi.method: Slow Tavi’s wheel until each splice can be felt
wire-tavi.speech: Finds the first click of the wheel with a seated hand.
wire-tavi.reply: The first click came through my hand before either of us heard it. Still got it.

quarter-matel.want: I patched sails before I kept hours. My tide clock keeps excellent time in a room without a boat.
quarter-matel.need: Walk Matel from the clock face to the actual waterline
quarter-matel.belief: A correct clock can give a boat the wrong instruction.
quarter-matel.method: Pin Matel’s strip of sailcloth at today's water mark
quarter-matel.speech: Reads the tide clock with a scrap of old sailcloth.
quarter-matel.reply: At the steps the sea was already in. The clock will get a second line of numbers.

grove-gresa-oker.want: I sing alto while I push saplings uphill. The little one at the back is the only one that gets the whole song.
grove-gresa-oker.need: Turn Gresa’s cart so the smallest sapling faces the yard
grove-gresa-oker.belief: Carrying living things makes the rehearsal wait its turn.
grove-gresa-oker.method: Hold Gresa’s back wheel through the last low note
grove-gresa-oker.speech: Tells a song in the order the cart's saplings hear it.
grove-gresa-oker.reply: The little tree made the turn without losing a leaf. So did my song.

door-neska.want: I put every guest to bed. Last night one asked which ballad I sing to get myself home.
door-neska.need: Save Neska a chair after the last guest goes upstairs
door-neska.belief: A keeper needs somebody to keep the end of a song for her.
door-neska.method: Pick up Neska’s answering line beside the night door
door-neska.speech: Offers an answering line from the far side of a night door.
door-neska.reply: I hadn't realised my homeward song had a second part until you took it.

door-tover.want: I carry soup till it's gone. I sing till my breath is gone. Yesterday I tried to do both down the stairs.
door-tover.need: Take one end of Tover’s pot at the steep stair
door-tover.belief: A generous offer still has to leave hands free for the work.
door-tover.method: Wait for Tover’s next breath before lifting the soup
door-tover.speech: Waits for a breath before asking somebody to lift the pot.
door-tover.reply: Two pairs of hands. One whole pot reached supper. I had breath left for the low note.

door-yilka.want: From my roof the harbour looks empty. I could hear the children under the awning the whole time.
door-yilka.need: Make room beside Yilka for a listener from the quay
door-yilka.belief: What the roof conceals can be common knowledge down on the stones.
door-yilka.method: Shade Yilka’s lamp and listen below the awning
door-yilka.speech: Gives the roof view time to answer the quay sound.
door-yilka.reply: A boy on the quay named three boats I couldn't see. He'll be up here with me next watch.

moth-runner-tritta.want: My moth will settle on any cap except the one I have just mended for it. There's gratitude for you.
moth-runner-tritta.need: Give Tritta’s moth a choice of two perches
moth-runner-tritta.belief: A creature can accept your company without accepting your plan.
moth-runner-tritta.method: Let Tritta’s two-tailed moth investigate the loose seam
moth-runner-tritta.speech: Lets a stubborn moth have the last word on a cap.
moth-runner-tritta.reply: She picked the unmended cap. Then she slept in my pocket all the way home.

river-emlet.want: I know the smell of a flour sack that's been in the post cart. Try putting that on a receipt.
river-emlet.need: Keep Emlet’s sample sack beside the baker’s till
river-emlet.belief: A remembered smell can tell you where to start asking for a receipt.
river-emlet.method: Open Emlet’s clean flour bag beside the posted one
river-emlet.speech: Reads a flour sack with a postman's remembered nose.
river-emlet.reply: The baker recognised that smell. He'd carried my old post bag as a boy.

river-rialla.want: Pendlow thinks I sort the letters by address. His I know by the smear of butter on the flap.
river-rialla.need: Give Rialla her brother’s unopened letter at the mooring
river-rialla.belief: Familiar hands leave traces a stranger could read differently.
river-rialla.method: Put Rialla’s two look-alike envelopes under the quay lamp
river-rialla.speech: Knows a brother's butter mark before opening the letter.
river-rialla.reply: Butter on the flap. An invitation to breakfast inside. It could hardly have been anything else.

river-pendlow.want: The oven skate sleeps against my warmest tin. If I'm late with the boat bread, everybody blames my sister.
river-pendlow.need: Save Pendlow a warm tin away from the delivery baskets
river-pendlow.belief: The person at the mooring is the last person to see what delayed the boat.
river-pendlow.method: Move Pendlow’s bread rack while the skate keeps its warm patch
river-pendlow.speech: Keeps one tin warm for a creature outside the delivery rota.
river-pendlow.reply: Skate asleep, rolls delivered, sister on time. I shall write that on the tin.

optics-nim.want: I still sew a spare button inside every lead coat. One day I'd like to be wearing it when it comes off.
optics-nim.need: Hold Nim’s place in the light while the button is sewn
optics-nim.belief: An understudy can know what a part needs before anybody hears the voice.
optics-nim.method: Pass Nim the wardrobe needle from the audience side
optics-nim.speech: Feels for a spare button before stepping into a lead's light.
optics-nim.reply: The button held through my bow. Nobody noticed. Imagine how properly pleased I am.

temple.1.agent.want: I painted the Y last night. I promised the boy he'd get to put in the two dots above the stall door.
temple.1.agent.need: Leave Mabry and the boy a brush each
temple.1.agent.belief: A child who can reach the receipt can decide whether to trust the stamp.
temple.1.agent.method: Let Mabry try the brass on the unstamped side
temple.1.agent.speech: Measures the cost of gold in letters on a stall sign.
temple.1.agent.reply: He painted one yellow dot and one blue. I shall be asked about them for the rest of my working life.

temple.1.guardian.want: There's still a dark patch by the little bowl. It's just where a short customer stands.
temple.1.guardian.need: Lower Brannoc’s spare lamp for the smallest visitor
temple.1.guardian.belief: A visitor's height changes the reach of my light.
temple.1.guardian.method: Hold Brannoc’s second wick under the brass lip
temple.1.guardian.speech: Counts what the light can reach from a child's height.
temple.1.guardian.reply: The boy saw his face in the bowl. He puffed his cheeks out at it. That's a successful inspection.

temple.2.agent.want: I'd like my dad to read the broken line aloud without trying to mend it in his head.
temple.2.agent.need: Sit with Wystan’s father over the torn line
temple.2.agent.belief: A gap that somebody can point to is easier to live with than a word they must pretend to see.
temple.2.agent.method: Put Wystan’s untrimmed slip on the reading desk
temple.2.agent.speech: Makes his father's next public reading the scale of a decision.
temple.2.agent.reply: Dad said “here's where it went.” Nobody laughed. One of the visitors pulled up a chair.

temple.2.guardian.want: I keep a little pin for the first child who notices the dates are on different leaves.
temple.2.guardian.need: Save Marrow a lower pin on the display
temple.2.guardian.belief: Two bits of reed can touch for centuries without sharing a birthday.
temple.2.guardian.method: Pass Marrow the later roll from the bottom shelf
temple.2.guardian.speech: Describes archival rank as the physical height of a reed hook.
temple.2.guardian.reply: The child noticed the space before either date. I had pinned my own eye too high.

temple.3.agent.want: I want my sister to see her whole name on something she can take home.
temple.3.agent.need: Give Osric a broad envelope and time to address it
temple.3.agent.belief: A cramped line tells you the clerk had little space. It tells you nothing about the size of a life.
temple.3.agent.method: Open Osric’s family slip at the uncut edge
temple.3.agent.speech: Fits a bureaucratic space around a sister's handwriting.
temple.3.agent.reply: She wrote very big indeed this time. We had to put the stamp on the other side.

temple.3.guardian.want: I promised to stay till the seed comes up. My legs could still do with an afternoon away.
temple.3.guardian.need: Take a watch at Mossgrave’s sister’s seed tray
temple.3.guardian.belief: A thing that sleeps leaves an observer with very little to count.
temple.3.guardian.method: Set Mossgrave’s two dated slips beside the seed tray
temple.3.guardian.speech: Holds open the length of a season for a seed.
temple.3.guardian.reply: There was nothing green when I got back. I was glad we'd both seen that day.

temple.4.agent.want: At the next bell I want a little girl on the quay to ask me her question herself.
temple.4.agent.need: Walk Astor to the quay before the teacher arrives
temple.4.agent.belief: A forecast changes when the person asking tells you what they need to save.
temple.4.agent.method: Set Astor’s vane at the height of the quay rail
temple.4.agent.speech: Starts with what a child needs to carry off the quay.
temple.4.agent.reply: She was worried about her wooden pony getting wet. I know just the shelf.

temple.4.guardian.want: I really did draw the child a graph. I wish I'd taken her shoes upstairs first.
temple.4.guardian.need: Carry the little pair of shoes up Halcy’s stair
temple.4.guardian.belief: A range alone cannot choose a dry landing.
temple.4.guardian.method: Mark Halcy’s flood line beside the lowest step
temple.4.guardian.speech: Translates the water range into a place for a pair of shoes.
temple.4.guardian.reply: A shoe fits on that step with a little room for a marble. Our graph had neither.

temple.5.agent.want: My brother's listening post has a crooked rung. I don't want them to repair it before he comes home.
temple.5.agent.need: Keep the carpenter’s mark beside Gale’s count
temple.5.agent.belief: Counting calls is a separate job from identifying callers.
temple.5.agent.method: Listen with Gale underneath the listening post
temple.5.agent.speech: Counts calls with one ear on the post a brother built.
temple.5.agent.reply: He made it crooked so my foot would fit. He'd forgotten. My foot hadn't.

temple.5.guardian.want: I'd like to count a whole dawn with somebody who never knew my sister's voice.
temple.5.guardian.need: Share the silent watch beside Ninefold
temple.5.guardian.belief: One bird can lend a whole wood its voice without growing a second throat.
temple.5.guardian.method: Watch Ninefold’s two reeds during one sustained call
temple.5.guardian.speech: Lets two counts stand beside a memory of a sister.
temple.5.guardian.reply: You heard one. I heard one and missed one. Best morning I've had in weeks.

temple.6.agent.want: Her method is on the page. Tonight I'd like her to walk through the door first.
temple.6.agent.need: Hold Harl’s guild door for the unnamed worker
temple.6.agent.belief: A method can travel into a book while its maker is kept outside.
temple.6.agent.method: Mark Harl’s comparison strip with its maker’s initials
temple.6.agent.speech: Asks whose feet can follow a method into the guild.
temple.6.agent.reply: They asked who she was. She answered by asking them for the tongs.

temple.6.guardian.want: I want the apprentice to hear what my elbow sounds like before the forge gets warm.
temple.6.guardian.need: Leave Grisel’s first cold strike out of the tally
temple.6.guardian.belief: An instrument can change between a worker's breakfast and dinner.
temple.6.guardian.method: Warm Grisel’s spare clamp before calling the next strike
temple.6.guardian.speech: Uses the morning note of an unreliable elbow to puncture certainty.
temple.6.guardian.reply: She heard my bad note and brought me a cup of tea. We tested the hammer afterwards.

temple.7.agent.want: I'd like the press to sleep long enough for the people who set the type to eat together.
temple.7.agent.need: Take Liesl’s turn at the idle press during supper
temple.7.agent.belief: A printer's name tells you who stood at the press. The line may have come a great deal further.
temple.7.agent.method: Turn Liesl’s amended sheet against the light
temple.7.agent.speech: Counts a silent press in missed suppers.
temple.7.agent.reply: They ate standing up from habit. Next time I shall hide the composing sticks.

temple.7.guardian.want: We have two perfectly good memories of one cup of coffee. Who will buy us another cup?
temple.7.guardian.need: Set two cups beside Mirro and Orrim’s unturned page
temple.7.guardian.belief: Even a shared accident may leave different stains on the two sides.
temple.7.guardian.method: Help the twins trace the coffee ring to its edge
temple.7.guardian.speech: Borrows a twin's memory and asks for the other side of the page.
temple.7.guardian.reply: My brother takes sugar. I don't. There's one part of the story we can still tell apart.

temple.8.agent.want: I'd like to hear our returning boat call my grandmother's reef by the little name she used.
temple.8.agent.need: Leave a quiet turn on Penrose’s radio
temple.8.agent.belief: One brief name saves breath. A second can guide a different boat home.
temple.8.agent.method: Carry Penrose’s chart to the sheltered side of the radio
temple.8.agent.speech: Gives a radio call in the breath left to a returning pilot.
temple.8.agent.reply: There it was between two calls for rope. I'd been listening for a grand announcement.

temple.8.guardian.want: I am saving my sister a place on the chart where there is room to write in her hand.
temple.8.guardian.need: Keep Saltmark’s clean chart open on the low table
temple.8.guardian.belief: Local pilots leave room to turn in a gap a printer wants to fill.
temple.8.guardian.method: Follow Saltmark’s unprinted bend with a finger
temple.8.guardian.speech: Reads the listening history behind a printed reef.
temple.8.guardian.reply: She drew a little fish before she wrote a word. We're leaving the fish.

temple.9.agent.want: I promised a caller an evening when she could just sit and clap.
temple.9.agent.need: Take Lucan’s handbell while the caller finds a seat
temple.9.agent.belief: A full house and a listening house make different silences.
temple.9.agent.method: Walk Lucan’s empty aisle after the house lights rise
temple.9.agent.speech: Hears an audience's held breath in empty chairs.
temple.9.agent.reply: She clapped in the wrong place on purpose. I could recognise her anywhere.

temple.9.guardian.want: The next chair I save is for the child who only knows the play from behind the kitchen wall.
temple.9.guardian.need: Move the Prompter’s spare cushion to the front rail
temple.9.guardian.belief: A cue heard through plaster belongs to a different performance.
temple.9.guardian.method: Replay the whispered cue from the Prompter’s working side
temple.9.guardian.speech: Speaks to the spectator who watched thirty years from the wings.
temple.9.guardian.reply: The child could say the whole play. Had never seen the blue coat. Started laughing at once.

temple.10.agent.want: One Saturday I'd like my mother to open her flour jar and find a loaf already waiting.
temple.10.agent.need: Carry Cass’s flour while her mother counts the empty jar
temple.10.agent.belief: A relief price should tell the relief worker what is missing as well as what is paid.
temple.10.agent.method: Weigh Cass’s wicker before it goes on sale
temple.10.agent.speech: Prices a relief decision from two household jars.
temple.10.agent.reply: She put half the loaf in the other jar. You can't beat her at this game.

temple.10.guardian.want: My scale has a beautiful brass cover. I've never once had to lift it with a baby on my hip.
temple.10.guardian.need: Let Quarta bring the basket to the buyer’s end
temple.10.guardian.belief: The reading ought to survive the everyday way somebody actually buys a loaf.
temple.10.guardian.method: Turn Quarta’s scale so both hands can reach the tare
temple.10.guardian.speech: Compares an even-handed balance with the cost of a loaf.
temple.10.guardian.reply: I had to put it down. The mother had been balancing everything on one little finger.

temple.11.agent.want: I would like my sister to answer just the last note. The rest of the song can wait.
temple.11.agent.need: Stand with Dorran through an unanswered verse
temple.11.agent.belief: A silent bank may be keeping time with you or asking you to stop.
temple.11.agent.method: Carry Dorran’s first call across the weir without a vote slip
temple.11.agent.speech: Lets a sung reply travel to the far bank in its own time.
temple.11.agent.reply: She opened her window. I managed to come home without calling that an answer.

temple.11.guardian.want: Three of us have spent a week on this meeting. Lull would like one afternoon to go fishing.
temple.11.guardian.need: Mind the three cups while Lull takes a turn on the bank
temple.11.guardian.belief: A neighbour's silence cannot sign a standing order for them.
temple.11.guardian.method: Turn the absent guardian’s cup sideways during the count
temple.11.guardian.speech: Three voices take turns disagreeing about the meaning of a cup.
temple.11.guardian.reply: Lull came back with an empty pail and an opinion. Brisk wrote them down separately.

temple.12.agent.want: I want our west-street postie to get home early for once. Our timetable says he already does.
temple.12.agent.need: Take Nyle’s last delivery with the west-street postie
temple.12.agent.belief: A route that looks quick at a desk can still spend someone's whole evening.
temple.12.agent.method: Walk Nyle’s last block before moving the starting peg
temple.12.agent.speech: Describes quiet streets from an unheard resident's doorstep.
temple.12.agent.reply: We got home late. The postie had supper waiting for both of us. He'd done the sums.

temple.12.guardian.want: I'd like the woman at the blue door to sign her own house into my model.
temple.12.guardian.need: Bring Ledgerlock’s little street out to the actual doorstep
temple.12.guardian.belief: The person who can open the door knows a detail my gears can't record.
temple.12.guardian.method: Fit Ledgerlock’s blue door from the resident’s side
temple.12.guardian.speech: Names the turn of every gear before admitting a house needs a name.
temple.12.guardian.reply: She turned the doorstep round. Our machine had had her stepping through the wall.

temple.13.agent.want: I want my family to leave a page closed for an afternoon without anyone guessing why.
temple.13.agent.need: Let Tolly’s family put away its page in peace
temple.13.agent.belief: A blank left by the teller belongs to a different person than a blank left by the keeper.
temple.13.agent.method: Offer Tolly’s spare slip to the original speaker
temple.13.agent.speech: Opens a family page only as far as its owners allow.
temple.13.agent.reply: They used the clean table to shell peas. A whole afternoon that belongs to nobody's catalogue.

temple.13.guardian.want: I want the owner of that breath to laugh at a different part of a recording for once.
temple.13.guardian.need: Wait for Hollin to hand the listening key back
temple.13.guardian.belief: A familiar voice is still somebody else's to lend.
temple.13.guardian.method: Play Hollin’s approved excerpt from the listener’s seat
temple.13.guardian.speech: Waits for permission in the middle of identifying a voice.
temple.13.guardian.reply: They played the wrong verse deliberately. First time I've heard the owner laugh on both sides of the box.

temple.14.agent.want: I'd like the child at the front to be the one who asks the lecturer where her model ends.
temple.14.agent.need: Hold Sabine’s pointer until the young questioner is ready
temple.14.agent.belief: A powerful model can keep the modeller's oldest question outside its frame.
temple.14.agent.method: Stand Sabine’s model beside the unmodelled house
temple.14.agent.speech: Remembers who brought the question after a lecture is over.
temple.14.agent.reply: The lecturer sat down on the floor. Apparently the child was the only one at the right height.

temple.14.guardian.want: My mother wants to pick the demonstration apple. She's never seen a blue ribbon worth eating.
temple.14.guardian.need: Save Tansy’s smallest tree for a family visit
temple.14.guardian.belief: The prize row and the row that fed a family can answer different questions.
temple.14.guardian.method: Place Tansy’s sample tray under the smallest tree
temple.14.guardian.speech: Tells a prize row and a family tree apart by their apples.
temple.14.guardian.reply: She chose the crooked apple. It was the only one she could get in her coat pocket.
